title: Create a Ride
summary: Pick public or private, set the day, time and meeting point, choose a mapped route or freeride, and share your new ride.
headings: How Many Rides You Can Create
text: You lead. Create a ride, tell everyone where and when to meet, and OnMyLead gives you a link, a code and a QR code to share. Public rides show up for riders nearby. Private rides are only for the people you invite. Create Your Ride On the Rides tab, tap Create a Ride . Under What Kind of Ride? , tap Public (open to anyone, found by riders near you or in your state) or Private (only friends you invite by link, text or email). Type a Ride Name . Under When , pick the day (see Pick the Day below). Type the time in Meet At , for example "8:00 am" or "2:30 pm". Set the Meeting Point . You can search in Search a Place or Address , tap Use My Current Location , or paste Coordinates like "38.57, -109.55". Add a Place Name if you like, such as "Gas station on Main St". Under The Route , tap Mapped (you draw the route or import a GPX file next) or Freeride (no set route, everyone follows the leader). Under Who's Riding , pick the Vehicles Welcome . Tap Create Public Ride or Create Private Ride . If you picked Mapped , the route builder opens right away so you can draw the trail. See Build a Route. Once the ride is saved you land on its page, ready to invite riders. Only riders who have joined see the exact meeting spot. Public pages show the general area, within about a mile. Pick the Day Under When , tap Today , Tomorrow or any day in the next two weeks. Public Ride Options A public ride is listed in its state so riders can find it. The State fills in from the meeting point. If it's wrong (it can happen near a border), tap Change State and pick the right one. Public rides also have a Joining choice: Anyone Can Join I Approve Riders See Approvals and the Waitlist for how requests work. Private rides don't have this choice: anyone holding your invite link or code can join. Limit Who Can Come Under Who's Riding , set Max Vehicles , Max Riders or both. Leave them empty for no limit. When the ride is full, new riders go on a waitlist. See Approvals and the Waitlist. Invite a Riding Group If you're in a riding group, an Invite a Group section shows up. Pick one or more groups under Your Riding Groups . Everyone in them gets a notification and sees the ride on their Rides tab, and they join with one tap. See Riding Groups. Add More Details Tap Add Route, Difficulty and More to fill in any of these: Description Departure Time and Expected Finish (used to check your ride against sunset, see Ride Day and Weather) Destination , which anyone who can see the ride sees, with directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps Route Length (Miles) , used to warn riders whose fuel range is too short (see Fuel Range) Difficulty : Easy, Moderate, Hard or Extreme Experience : Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced or Expert What to Bring , Required Equipment and Fuel Instructions for Joined Riders , which only riders on the ride see Ride Bubble : Standard, Tight Trail, Desert or Highway (see Ride Bubble) After You Create It Your ride page opens with a card that has the invite code, a QR code and buttons to share it. See Invite Riders. You're also the ride's organizer and leader. See Organizer Controls. How Many Rides You Can Create Free accounts create one ride each month. Joining rides is always free and unlimited. On Free, the top of the Create a Ride screen shows Rides Created This Month so you know where you stand. When you've used this month's free ride, the app tells you the date your next one opens (the first of the month, UTC). Creating more rides than that is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. A ride counts toward the month you create it, even if you later cancel or delete it. Copying a ride or using Ride Again also creates a new ride. Pro bought on Android through Google Play lifts the monthly limit the same way, on every device you sign in to.

title: Create and Manage a Riding Group
summary: Save the people you ride with as a group, invite friends with a link, and invite the whole group to a ride in one tap.
headings: Invite Friends With the Group Link
Invite Your Group to a Ride
Remove a Rider, Leave or Delete a Group
text: A riding group is your regular crew, saved once. When you create a ride, you can invite everyone in the group in one tap instead of sending the invite to each rider. Each group also has its own Group Chat. Your groups live on the Groups tab, on the Riding Groups screen. It shows Your Groups (the ones you run) and Groups You’re In (the ones someone else runs). This is a Pro feature. You need Pro to create a group and to add or remove riders. See Free and Pro. Joining a group with its link, the group chat, inviting a group to your rides and getting the group's ride invites are free for everyone. Create a Group Tap the Groups tab. Tap New Group . Type a Group Name , like Saturday Crew. Names can be up to 60 characters. Under Add Riders You’ve Ridden With , tick the riders you want in the group. Tap Save Group . The list only shows people you have been on a ride with, the ones you ride with most at the top. If nobody shows up yet, save the group anyway and send friends the group link (see below). A group holds up to 100 riders. Invite Friends With the Group Link The group link is for friends who aren't on OnMyLead yet, or anyone you haven't ridden with. Anyone in the group can share it. On the Groups tab, tap the group. Scroll to Invite by Link . Tap Share Group Link , or tap Text , Email or Copy . When your friend opens the link, they see the group's name, who runs it and how many riders are in it. They don't see who the riders are until they join. They tap Join Group , or Create a Free Account to Join if they don't have an account yet. If a link got shared somewhere it shouldn't, the rider who runs the group can tap Make a New Link . The old link stops working, and everyone already in the group stays in. Add More Riders If you run the group: Open the group. Tap Add Riders You’ve Ridden With . Tick the riders and tap Add Riders . Invite Your Group to a Ride You can invite a group you're in to any upcoming ride you organize or co-organize. There are two ways. From the group: Open the group. Tap Invite to a Ride . Tap Invite next to the ride. From the ride: Open the ride and go to Riders . Under Invite a Group , tap Invite All next to the group. Everyone in the group gets a notification and sees the ride under Ride Invites on their home screen. They can tap Join Ride , with no waiting for approval, or No Thanks . Riders who are already on the ride, waiting, or who said no thanks are left alone. To get these invites, keep Ride Invites on in Notification Settings. Rename a Group If you run the group, open it, tap the group's name, type the new name and tap Save Name . Remove a Rider, Leave or Delete a Group Remove a rider: if you run the group, tap Remove next to the rider. They stop getting the group's ride invites. You can add them back later. Leave a group: open the group and tap Leave Group . The group link brings you back if you change your mind. Delete a group: if you run the group, tap Delete Group . The group goes away for everyone in it. Rides you already invited it to stay as they are. Who Can See a Group A group's name and who is in it are only visible to the rider who runs it and the riders in it. The group link only shows the name, who runs it and how many riders are in it. If your Pro ends, your groups stay. Everyone in them can still chat, and you can still invite the group to your rides. Creating new groups and adding or removing riders needs Pro again.

title: Draw a Route
summary: Tap the map to lay down your ride's route. It snaps to trails for you, and every rider sees it in Ride Mode.
headings: Check Who Can Ride a Trail
text: A route is the line your group will follow. Once it's saved, every rider on the ride sees it on the ride page and in Ride Mode, with everyone placed along it. You draw it by tapping points on a satellite map, and OnMyLead follows the trails between your taps for you. Drawing a route is free. Bringing one in from a GPX file is covered in Import a GPX Route. Who Can Draw the Route The ride's organizer and any co-organizers can build or change the route, until the ride has ended or been cancelled. Everyone else on the ride sees the finished route but can't change it. See Organizer Controls. Open the Route Builder When you create a ride and pick Mapped under The Route , the route builder opens as soon as the ride is created. To open it later: Open the ride and tap the Map tab. Tap Build the Route . If the ride already has a route, tap Edit Route . For a Freeride, tap Map a Route Anyway . A Freeride that gets a saved route becomes a mapped ride. Draw Your Route The map opens at the ride's meeting point. Tap the map where the ride starts. That's point 1, shown in green. To get there fast, tap Search at the top and type a trailhead, park or town. Tap further along the trail. The route follows the trail between your two taps. Keep tapping along the way. Each new point is numbered, and the last one is shown in white. Watch the miles add up at the top of the panel at the bottom of the screen. Tap Save Route when you're done. After you save, you're taken back to the ride. Only riders on this ride can see the route. Follow Trails or Straight Line Two choices in the panel decide how the next points are joined: Follow Trails : each tap lands on the nearest trail or road, and the line between taps runs along it. While it works this out you'll see a dashed straight line and Finding the trail… . Straight Line : draws straight from point to point. Use it for open ground, a wash or a park nobody has mapped. You can switch between them as you go. Points you already placed keep the way they were drawn. The app remembers your choice for next time. If no mapped trail joins two points, that part is drawn as a straight line and the app tells you so. Add a point on the trail, or zoom in and try again. Points very far apart are also joined with a straight line, so tap more often on long stretches. Trails come from OpenStreetMap, so snapping works best where riders have mapped the trails. Zooming in before you tap helps each point land on the trail you meant. Fix Mistakes Undo takes back the last point. Drag any numbered point to move it. If the line next to it was following a trail, it snaps again. Clear removes every point. Nothing is saved until you tap Save Route . To see more of the map, swipe the panel down or tap its handle. It folds down to the miles and an Undo button. Search for a Place To jump the map to a trailhead, park, forest or town before you draw: Tap Search at the top of the screen. Type a name, an address or coordinates. Tap a result. The map moves there and marks it. Searching only moves the map. Nothing is added to your route. See Search for a Place. Check Who Can Ride a Trail While drawing, a tap adds a point, so press and hold a trail line instead to see its name and which vehicles it's open to. You can also turn trail lines on or off and switch to a topo map with the layers button. See Map Layers and Trails. Change or Remove a Route Open the ride, tap the Map tab, and tap Edit Route . Move, add or undo points, then tap Save Route . To take the route off the ride, tap Clear , confirm, then tap Remove Route . When you save a route, the ride's listed miles update to match it. On the Website You can build the route at onmylead.com too, using the same steps: Click the map instead of tapping, and drag a point to move it. Press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac) to undo the last point. Trail lines and their names appear once you zoom in close, and Follow Trails snaps to them the same way. On a wide screen, the tools panel sits beside the map. On a

title: Find a Ride
summary: Browse public rides near you, near a place you search, or anywhere in a state, on a map or in a list.
text: Looking for people to ride with? The Find tab shows public rides near you or anywhere in a state. Private rides never show here. You need an invite link or code for those. See Join a Ride. Find Rides Near You Tap the Find tab (or Find a Ride on the Rides tab). Make sure Near Me is selected at the top. Allow location if asked. If location is off, tap Use My Location , or pick your state instead. Under How Far Will You Go? , pick 25 Miles , 50 Miles , 100 Miles or 250 Miles . Rides show on the map and in a list under it, nearest first, with how far away each one is. Find Rides Near a Place Planning a trip somewhere else? Search a park, trailhead or town. On the Find tab, tap Search Near a Place . Type the place and pick it from the results. The list shows Rides Near that place. Tap Back to Near Me to go back to rides around you. Find Rides in a State On the Find tab, tap By State . Pick a state. Rides in that state show soonest first. To switch states, tap the state's name in the corner of the map. Use the Map Each dot is a ride. Blue dots are upcoming rides. Red, glowing dots are live now. Tap a dot to see the ride's name, time and distance, then tap Open Ride . Move or zoom the map, then tap Search This Area to see rides there. To return, tap the button under the map that starts with Back to , such as Back to Rides Near Me . Use the + and - buttons to zoom, and the location button to recenter the map. On a wide screen, such as the website on a computer, the search and the list of rides sit on the left and the map fills the rest of the screen. Dots sit on the ride's general meeting area, within about a mile. The exact meeting spot is shown only to riders who join. What You'll See Find shows public rides that are coming up or live right now. Each ride in the list shows its date, time, general area, difficulty, distance and the vehicles welcome. Tap a ride to open its page and join. See Join a Ride. If there are no rides yet, tap Create a Public Ride to start one. See Create a Ride. The Rides tab also lists a few upcoming Public Rides . Tap Find Rides on the Map (or See All on the Map , which shows how many there are) to see them all.

title: Fix Common Problems
summary: What to check when riders don't show on the map, alerts don't arrive, a download stops or sign-in fails.
headings: A Rider Shows as a Hollow Dot or "Last Seen"
My Group Can't See Me With My Phone Locked
I Tapped a Status Button With No Signal
Part of My Route Is a Straight Line
I Turned On Trails but See No Lines
I Don't See a Fuel Check on My Ride
My Password Reset Link Says It Has Expired
The Starlink Page Can't Reach My Dish
text: Start here when something doesn't work the way you expect. If your problem isn't listed, contact us. A Rider Shows as a Hollow Dot or "Last Seen" A rider's dot turns hollow when their last position is more than a minute old, and shows No Signal with a dashed grey ring after about 3 minutes. A sharing phone checks in at least every 15 seconds while it has service, so this usually means that rider lost service. If everyone suddenly shows as last seen, it's probably your phone. After about 35 seconds without hearing from the server, Ride Mode shows No Service. Riders Show Where They Were Last Seen . It doesn't mark the others as lost because of your own dropout. See Share Your Location. My Group Can't See Me With My Phone Locked Open your iPhone's Settings OnMyLead Location . Choose Always . Open Ride Mode again. If your share is still running, it picks back up. On Android, check that the Sharing Your Location notification is showing while you share. If it isn't, open Ride Mode again to restart it. If your phone has a battery saver that closes apps, set OnMyLead's battery use to Unrestricted in Settings Apps OnMyLead Battery . Closing Ride Mode or locking your phone doesn't stop sharing. Sharing ends when your timer runs out, the ride ends, you leave the ride, or you tap Stop . I Tapped a Status Button With No Signal It waits on your phone as Waiting for Signal and sends by itself as soon as you have service, stamped with the time you tapped it. You can tap Retry Now or Cancel . See Status Buttons. I'm Not Getting Alerts Check that notifications are allowed for OnMyLead in your iPhone's Settings Notifications OnMyLead . In the app, open You and check your notification settings, including quiet hours. On Android, check Settings Apps OnMyLead Notifications , including the Rider Alerts , Ride Chat and Ride Updates categories. Need Help and EMERGENCY alerts from your group always come through, even in quiet hours, as long as iPhone notifications are allowed for OnMyLead. Part of My Route Is a Straight Line The route builder follows mapped trails. It draws a straight line when no mapped trail joins two points, when the points are very far apart, or when you had no signal and that trail data wasn't saved on your phone. Add a point on the trail or zoom in, or use Straight Line for unmapped ground. See Draw a Route. I Turned On Trails but See No Lines Zoom in. Forest Service and BLM lines appear from about zoom level 9 ( Zoom In to See Trails ), and smaller park and local tracks need you to zoom in further ( Zoom In for Park and Local Trails ). The website shows fewer trail layers than the app. See Map Layers. My Offline Map Download Stopped Closing the app pauses a running download. Open You Offline Maps and tap Resume , or Finish if some pieces are missing. If the area says Too big for one download , zoom in so the frame covers less. See Offline Maps. I Don't See a Fuel Check on My Ride The fuel check needs miles to check against (a saved route or Route Length (Miles) ) and a machine in your Garage with Tank (gal) and Miles per Gallon filled in. If you have more than one machine, pick yours under Bringing on the ride. See Fuel Range. My Password Reset Link Says It Has Expired Reset links work once and expire. Tap Back to Sign In , ask for a new link, and open it on the same iPhone. See Sign In. The Starlink Page Can't Reach My Dish Your iPhone has to be on the Starlink Wi-Fi, and OnMyLead needs Local Network access ( Settings OnMyLead ). The page tries again every 10 seconds. It doesn't work on the website. See Starlink.

title: Free and Pro
summary: What every OnMyLead account gets for free, what OnMyLead Pro adds, and how the Free monthly ride works.
text: OnMyLead is free to download and use. Free accounts can join as many rides as they like, and every safety feature is free on every plan. OnMyLead Pro is for riders who lead a lot of rides and want extras like offline maps and GPX import. Pro is $4.99 a month or $29.99 a year in the US. Other countries see the price in local currency. Every new account starts with a free 30-day Pro Trial. What's Included This is the same comparison as the Free and Pro table on the Pro screen. Free Pro --- --- --- Create Rides 1 a Month Unlimited Join Rides Unlimited Unlimited Live Tracking, SOS and Ride Bubble Yes Yes Ride Chat and Voting Yes Yes Draw Routes and Follow Leaders Yes Yes Import GPX Routes No Yes Offline Maps No Yes Saved Riding Groups No Yes Create Ride Polls No Yes Ride History Last 5 All Advanced Trip Planning No Yes Advanced Ride Statistics No Yes Premium Ride Cards No Yes Always Free Safety never depends on your plan. On every plan you get Ride Mode, live tracking, Need Help, EMERGENCY, Mechanical Issue alerts, Ride Bubble, location sharing, family links, ride chat and joining rides. The Free Monthly Ride Free accounts create one ride each calendar month. The month follows UTC time, so a new month can start a few hours earlier or later than midnight where you live. A ride counts when you create it. Deleting or cancelling it doesn't give the ride back. Using Ride Again to copy a ride counts as creating a ride. Rides you create on the website count too. Joining other riders' rides is always unlimited. When you create a ride on a Free account, the Create a Ride screen shows how many you've created this month, like Rides Created This Month: 0 of 1 . If you've used it, the app tells you the date your next free ride opens, and you can tap See OnMyLead Pro or Not Now . What Each Pro Feature Does Create More Rides: Pro creates as many rides as you lead. Import GPX Routes: bring in a track from Gaia, onX or any GPX file. See Import a GPX Route. Drawing a route on the map stays free, and a route you already imported stays editable. Offline Maps: download satellite, topo and trail maps so the map keeps working with no signal. See Offline Maps. Maps already on your phone keep working on Free. Saved Riding Groups: save your crew, add riders and invite everyone in one tap. See Riding Groups. Joining a group, its chat and its ride invites stay free. Create Ride Polls: ask the group a quick question in ride chat. Everyone can still vote on polls for free. See Ride Polls. Full Ride History: Free shows your last 5 past rides. Pro shows every ride you've been on. Nothing is ever deleted, so older rides come back if you upgrade. Advanced Trip Planning: plan several trips at once, start from packing lists, copy trips and link them to rides. One active trip and the fuel check stay free. See Trip Planner. Advanced Ride Statistics: moving time, average and top speed, climbing and the group's totals after every ride. Distance and time out stay free. Premium Ride Cards: share your ride with the Full Stats and Big Number layouts. The standard card stays free. When you tap something that needs Pro, a short prompt explains it. Tap See OnMyLead Pro to see the plans, or Not Now to close it. See Your Plan On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Your Plan shows Free, Pro Trial or Pro. On Free it also shows how many rides you've created this month. Your plan is saved on your phone, so the app knows it even with no signal. Pro is bought in the app on iPhone or iPad through the App Store. Pro you buy there also works when you use OnMyLead on the website. On Android, Pro is bought through Google Play. Pro belongs to your OnMyLead account, so it works on iPhone, iPad, Android and the website, whichever store you bought it from.

title: Get Started With OnMyLead
summary: What OnMyLead is, how to get the app on iPhone, iPad or Android, make your account, and find your way around the Rides, Find, Groups and You tabs.
text: OnMyLead is a group ride app for off-road riders. The leader creates a ride, the crew joins with a code, link or QR code, and on the trail everyone shares one live map, a group chat and quick taps like Need Fuel and Flat Tire that tell the whole group at once. Get the App OnMyLead runs on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets. Download OnMyLead free from the App Store on an iPhone or iPad, or from Google Play on an Android phone or tablet, then open it. It's the same account, rides and Pro plan on every device, and iPhone and Android riders ride together on the same map. Make Your Account You can look around without an account, but you need one to create rides, save your Garage and keep riding groups. On the Rides tab, tap Sign In or Create a Free Account . Tap Create Account at the top. Use one of the Continue with buttons, or enter Your Name , Email and a Password of at least 8 characters, then tap Create Account . If we email you a link, tap it on the same iPhone to confirm your email and finish signing in. See Sign In and Create an Account for every way to sign in. Next, pick your ride name. It's what other riders see on the map, the rider list and in chat. Until you pick one, Home shows Pick Your Ride Name and other riders see you as Rider. See Your Ride Name and Profile. New accounts start with a free Pro Trial. See The Pro Trial. Find Your Way Around Four tabs run along the bottom of the screen. On a tablet they run down the left edge instead. See Use OnMyLead on a Tablet. Rides Your home screen. Create a Ride : start a ride that you lead. Free accounts create one ride a month. See Create a Ride and Free and Pro. Join a Ride : type an invite code and tap Open . See Join a Ride. Find a Ride : opens the Find tab. When one of your rides is live, a card at the top says Your ride is live. Tap to open Ride Mode . Ride Invites , Your Rides and Past Rides list the rides you're on. Swipe a ride left to delete it (if you organize it) or leave it. On onmylead.com, click Delete or Leave at the end of the row instead. The app always asks first. Public Rides shows a few upcoming public rides near the bottom. Find Public rides on a map. Choose Near Me or By State , or use Search Near a Place to look around a trailhead, park or town. See Find a Ride. Groups Your riding groups, the groups you're in, and Leaders You Follow . Tap New Group to save your crew. You need an account for this tab; if you're signed out, it takes you to sign in. See Riding Groups. You Everything that isn't a ride: Your ride name and plan at the top. Your Gear : Garage, Trip Planner and Offline Maps. On the Trail : Share My Location and Starlink. Settings : Notifications, Directions (which maps app Navigate opens), Subscription and Blocked Riders . Account : the email you sign in with. Help : Contact Us and Help and Support . Sign Out and Delete Account at the bottom. Permissions the App Asks For Notifications After you sign in, your iPhone asks if OnMyLead can send notifications. Say yes so you hear when someone in your group taps Need Help or EMERGENCY , even with the phone in your pocket. Tapping a notification opens the ride it is about. You choose everything else in Notification Settings. Location OnMyLead asks for your location when you first use it, for example to find rides near you or when you start sharing on a ride. Your location is shared only with riders you choose, only while you're sharing. When you share on a ride, your iPhone may also ask to allow location Always . Allow it so your group keeps seeing you while your phone is locked on the mount. Sharing always stops when your timer ends or the ride ends. See Location Sharing. On Android, allow location While Using the App . OnMyLead never asks for Allow All the Time : while you share, Android shows a Sharing Your Location notification, and that keeps your group updated with the phone locked. On Android 13 and later, allow notifications too, so you can see that notification and hear Need

title: Share Your Location
summary: Choose who sees your location and for how long. Sharing always ends on its own, and you can stop it any time.
headings: Share with Chosen Riders or Family
text: OnMyLead only shares your location when you turn it on, only with the people you choose, and only for as long as you pick. Every share ends on its own. These rules are enforced by OnMyLead's server, not just the app. There are two ways to share: With a ride: everyone on the ride sees you on the Ride Mode map. With chosen people: riders you pick, a family link, or both, from Share My Location . Share with Your Ride When you open Ride Mode on a live ride and aren't sharing yet, the app asks Share Your Location with This Ride? Open Ride Mode. See Use Ride Mode. Pick how long to share: 2 Hours , 4 Hours , 8 Hours or Until I Leave the Ride . Or type your own length in Hours and tap Share . The longest you can pick is 24 hours. If your iPhone asks for location access, allow it. Choose Always so the group keeps seeing you with the phone locked. Only riders on this ride see you. Tap Not Now to skip. You can start sharing later by tapping the Off pill at the top of Ride Mode. Check or Stop Ride Sharing The pill at the top of Ride Mode shows the time left, such as 1h 20m , or On when you picked Until I Leave the Ride . Tap the pill. A banner shows Sharing and the time left. Tap Stop to stop sharing now, or Hide to fold the banner back into the pill. When Ride Sharing Ends Sharing with a ride stops on its own at the first of these: Your timer runs out. The organizer ends or cancels the ride. You leave the ride. You tap Stop . Closing Ride Mode, or locking your phone, doesn't stop sharing. If the app was closed or your phone restarted, opening Ride Mode picks your share back up. Share with Chosen Riders or Family Tap the You tab. Under On the Trail , tap Share My Location . Under Who Can See You , tap the riders you want. Only people you've been on a ride with are listed. To share with someone who doesn't have the app, turn on Family Link . See Share a Family Link. Under For How Long , pick 15 Min , 1 Hour , 4 Hours , 8 Hours or Until I Turn It Off (Max 24 Hours) , or type your own length in Hours and tap Share . Until I Turn It Off still stops by itself after 24 hours, so a forgotten share always ends. While you share, Share My Location shows a card for each share with Sharing Now and the time left. Tap Add 1 Hour to keep going longer. In the last 10 minutes, the button says Ending Soon · Add 1 Hr . Tap Stop to end it now. Location in the Background To keep your group updated while your phone is locked or in your pocket, OnMyLead needs location access set to Always . You can change it any time in your iPhone's Settings OnMyLead Location . While OnMyLead is using your location in the background, iPhone shows its location indicator. On Android, allow location While Using the App . OnMyLead doesn't need Allow All the Time . While you share, Android shows a Sharing Your Location notification, and that is what keeps your group updated with the phone locked. Tap it to see who can see you or to stop sharing. On Android 13 and later, also allow notifications when asked, or that notification stays hidden. Your phone sends a new position each time you move about 25 meters (80 feet), and at least every 15 seconds while you're stopped, so the group can tell you're still there. With No Service Live tracking needs a connection. When your phone has no service: The group sees where you were last seen, with how long ago, never a dot that looks live. While you share with a ride, your phone keeps recording your track. When you get service again, your current position goes up, and the points from the dead zone are added to your ride track for your ride summary. Sharing still ends at its end time, even if your phone can't reach the server. Offline maps keep the map on your screen without service, but positions only update when phones have a connection. See Offline Maps. Who Sees What Ride sharing: riders who have joined that ride. Chosen riders: only the riders you picked are allowed to see your position. title: Sign In and Create an Account
summary: Sign in with Apple, Google or Facebook, an email and password, or an emailed sign-in link, and reset a forgotten password.
headings: Sign In With Apple, Google or Facebook
Create an Account With Email and a Password
Sign In With Email and a Password
Sign In With an Email Link (No Password)
Opening an Email Link on Another Device
text: You need an account to create rides, keep a Garage and save riding groups. You can sign in with a social account, with your email and a password, or with a link we email you. Open the Sign-In Screen On the Rides tab or the You tab, tap Sign In or Create a Free Account . At the top, choose Sign In if you already have an account, or Create Account if you're new. Tapping something that needs an account, like the Groups tab, also opens this screen. Sign In With Apple, Google or Facebook Depending on what's turned on, you'll see Continue with Apple , Continue with Google and Continue with Facebook at the top of the screen. Tap the button for the account you want to use. Follow the steps on the Apple, Google or Facebook screen. You're signed in and taken back to OnMyLead. If you were new, your account is created. With Apple, the name on your Apple Account is used as your ride name the first time you sign in, if Apple shares it. You can change it any time. See Your Ride Name and Profile. On the website, Continue with Apple may not be there. Use Apple in the iPhone app, or sign in on the website another way. Create an Account With Email and a Password Tap Create Account at the top. Enter Your Name . This is what riders will see, and you can change it later. Enter your Email . Enter a Password of at least 8 characters. Tap Create Account . If the app says Almost done , open the email we sent and tap the link on the same iPhone. Your email is confirmed and you're signed in. Sign In With Email and a Password Tap Sign In at the top. Enter your Email and Password . Tap Sign In . Sign In With an Email Link (No Password) Enter your Email . Tap Or email me a sign-in link instead (no password) . Open the email on the same iPhone and tap the link. The link signs you in and opens Home, even if the sign-in screen was still open. If you don't have an account yet, it creates one. Reset a Forgotten Password Tap Sign In at the top. Enter your Email . Tap Forgot your password? Email me a reset link . Open the email on your iPhone and tap the link. Enter a New Password of at least 8 characters. Tap Save Password . If you see This Link Has Expired , tap Back to Sign In and ask for a new reset link. Opening an Email Link on Another Device If you tap a link from us in a browser on an iPhone, you may see Open OnMyLead . Tap Open in the App to finish in the app, or Continue on the Website to stay in the browser. If you see Your Email Is Confirmed and a request to sign in again, the link opened somewhere other than where you signed up. Your email is confirmed. Tap Sign In and sign in once more with your email and password. Sign Out Go to the You tab. Scroll down and tap Sign Out . This signs you out on this device only. If you're also signed in on another device or the website, you stay signed in there, and any location you're sharing from that device keeps going. If Something Goes Wrong That email and password don't match : check for typos, or use the reset link above. Please confirm your email first : tap the link in the email we sent you, then sign in. There's already an account with that email : switch to Sign In at the top. Too many emails sent just now : wait a few minutes and try again. That Link Didn't Work : the link expired or was already used. Tap Back to Sign In and ask for a new one. Still stuck? Contact Us and pick Account and Sign-In .

title: Use Ride Mode
summary: The live group map for ride day. See every rider, who is live and who was last seen, where you are on the route, and the one-tap buttons.
headings: See Where You Are on the Route
Fold the Panel to See More Map
text: Ride Mode is the screen you use on the trail. It puts the whole group on one map, shows how fresh each rider's position is, places everyone along the route, and gives you big one-tap buttons for telling the group what's going on. Ride Mode is free on every plan. Open Ride Mode Ride Mode opens once the organizer starts the ride. Organizers: on the ride page, tap Start Ride Mode . The ride goes live for everyone and Ride Mode opens. Riders: once the ride is live, open the ride page and tap Enter Ride Mode . Riders on the ride also get a notification when the ride starts. The first time you open Ride Mode on a ride, it asks Share Your Location with This Ride? Pick how long to share, or tap Not Now . You can see the group without sharing, but the group can't see you. See Share Your Location. Your screen stays on while Ride Mode is open, so the map is ready when you glance at it. Keep a charger handy on long rides. What's on the Screen The Top Bar ‹ Ride name: tap it to go back to the ride page. The sharing pill: shows how long you have left sharing, such as 1h 20m , or On when there's no timer. It says Off when you aren't sharing; tap it to start. While you share, tap it to show Sharing, 1 hr 20 min left with Stop and Hide . Together or 2 Separated: green when the group is together, red with a count when Ride Bubble sees riders who have dropped away. Tap it to open the Riders list. The Map The map shows the ride's route, waypoints, planned stops and any regroup point. Every rider who is sharing shows as a dot with their ride name beside it. The leader is the one bigger blue dot, so you can find them at a glance. Tap a rider's dot to see their name, whether they're live, and their latest status. You don't need to leave Ride Mode to see new riders. Someone who joins the ride while you're on the map appears within a few seconds of starting to share, and a rider whose share ends or who leaves the ride drops off the map within about 15 seconds. To switch map layers or download the ride's map for riding with no signal, use the layers button on the map. See Map Layers and Offline Maps. The Bottom Panel The panel at the bottom holds the route strip, alert cards, the quick replies and the status buttons. See Status Buttons and Quick Replies. Above the panel are two buttons: Directions (on the left) for Apple Maps or Google Maps, and Add Waypoint (on the right) to mark your spot. You can also press and hold anywhere on the map to drop a waypoint there. See Get Directions and Waypoints and Planned Stops. On Android, Directions opens Google Maps, and while you share, a Sharing Your Location notification stays in the notification shade. Tap it to come back to OnMyLead. If your phone restarted or the app was updated while you were sharing, opening Ride Mode starts that notification and your sharing again. Read the Rider Dots A dot only looks live when the phone behind it is actually checking in. A sharing phone sends its position at least every 15 seconds while it has service, even when it's parked. What you see What it means --- --- Solid dot Live. The position is less than a minute old. Hollow dot with Last Seen 2 Min Ago Where the rider was last seen, a minute or more ago. Dashed grey ring with No Signal, 8 Min Ago Nothing for three minutes or more. Their phone has likely lost service or stopped sending. Faint ring, Not Sharing The rider is on the ride but isn't sharing their location. Yellow or red ring around a dot Ride Bubble thinks the rider is separating from the group. Amber wrench on a dot The rider tapped Mechanical Issue . See Every Rider Tap Together (or Separated ) at the top to open the Riders list. It shows everyone on the ride, the leader first, with Live , Last Seen and an age, No Signal , or Not Sharing . The leader and tail gunner are labeled. Tap Navigate next to a live rider, or Go to Last Seen for a rider whose spot is old, to get directions to them in your maps app. See Where You Are on the Route When the ride has a rout

title: Create a Ride on the Website
summary: Plan a ride on onmylead.com from your computer, drop the meeting point on a map, and find it in the app on your phone as soon as you save.
headings: Create a Ride on the Web
Draw the Route on the Web
text: You can plan a ride on the big screen at onmylead.com. It's the same ride as one made in the app: the ride, its route and its stops show up in the OnMyLead app on your phone or tablet as soon as you save. Ride Mode and live tracking stay in the app. Create a Ride on the Web Go to onmylead.com and click Create a Ride on the Web . Sign in with your OnMyLead account if you aren't already. You go straight to Create a Ride after signing in. Pick Public or Private under What Kind of Ride? Fill in the Ride Name , the day under When , and the Meet At time. Click Calendar to pick any day from today up to a year out. Set the Meeting Point : type a park, trailhead, town or address in Search a Place or Address (just above the map) and pick it, or click the satellite map to drop the pin, then drag the pin to fine-tune it. You can also use your location or type coordinates, and the pin moves there. Under The Route , pick Mapped or Freeride . Fill in anything else you want, then click Create Public Ride or Create Private Ride . The rest of the form works the same as in the app. See Create a Ride for every option. Draw the Route on the Web If you picked Mapped , the route builder opens after you create the ride. Click along the trail and the route follows it. Drawing a route is free. Importing a GPX file is a Pro feature. See Build a Route and Free and Pro. To find a trailhead or park by name while you draw, click Search at the top of the map and pick a result. The map jumps there. You can also add numbered planned stops for fuel, lunch or camp. See Waypoints and Planned Stops. Share It After saving, your ride page shows the invite code, a QR code and share buttons, the same as in the app. See Invite Riders. Free accounts create one ride each month, whether on the website or in the app. See Free and Pro. When someone opens a ride link on a computer, the page shows the ride's QR code. They can scan it with their phone's camera to open the ride on their phone. Stuck while planning? Click Help at the top of onmylead.com to open these guides.

title: Frequently Asked Questions
summary: Quick answers about free rides, the Pro Trial, privacy, editing rides, iPhone, iPad and Android, and the website.
headings: I Deleted the Ride I Made This Month. Can I Make Another on Free?
Will I Be Charged When My Pro Trial Ends?
My Pro Trial Ended Mid-Month and I Can't Create a Ride. Why?
Can I Buy Pro or Use a Promo Code on the Website?
Does Deleting My Account Cancel My Pro Subscription?
Can I Change My Ride's Time or Meeting Point?
My Ride Still Says Live. How Do I End It?
Why Can't I See the Exact Meeting Spot?
Why Isn't My Ride Showing on Find?
Why Do Other Riders See Me as "Rider"?
Does "Until I Turn It Off" Sharing Ever End?
Does Live Tracking Work With No Cell Service?
Can I Use OnMyLead on an iPad or Android Phone?
How Many Waypoints Can I Add?
text: Is OnMyLead Free? Yes. Free accounts create one ride each calendar month and can join as many rides as they like, and the safety features are always free. OnMyLead Pro adds unlimited rides and more. I Deleted the Ride I Made This Month. Can I Make Another on Free? No. A ride counts when it's created, so cancelling or deleting it doesn't give it back, and copying a ride or using Ride Again counts as a new ride. Your next free ride opens on the 1st of next month (UTC). Will I Be Charged When My Pro Trial Ends? No. The Pro Trial needs no payment and never turns into a paid subscription. Your account moves to Free, and your rides, routes, groups and maps stay. My Pro Trial Ended Mid-Month and I Can't Create a Ride. Why? Rides you created during the trial count toward that month's one free ride. Can I Buy Pro or Use a Promo Code on the Website? No. Subscribing, Restore Purchases and promo codes work only in the app on your phone or tablet. Pro bought in the app also works when you sign in on the website. Does Deleting My Account Cancel My Pro Subscription? No. Apple bills Pro, so also cancel it in your Apple subscriptions so you aren't billed again. See Manage Your Subscription. If you bought Pro on Android, Google Play bills it: cancel it in Google Play too. Can I Change My Ride's Time or Meeting Point? Not after it's created. Tap Copy This Ride to make a new ride with the same details and route, pick the new day, then cancel the old ride. See Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride. My Ride Still Says Live. How Do I End It? Rides don't end on their own. The organizer taps End Ride for Everyone on the ride page. Ending a ride stops everyone's location sharing for that ride. Why Can't I See the Exact Meeting Spot? Only riders who have joined see it. Before you join, you see the general area, within about a mile. See Privacy. Why Isn't My Ride Showing on Find? Find lists only public rides that are upcoming or live. Private rides never appear there, and rides drop off a few hours after their meeting time. See Find a Ride. Why Do Other Riders See Me as "Rider"? You haven't picked a ride name yet. Tap Pick Your Ride Name on the Rides tab, or your name at the top of You . See Your Ride Name and Profile. Does "Until I Turn It Off" Sharing Ever End? Yes. Personal shares stop by themselves after 24 hours. A ride share set to Until I Leave the Ride ends when the ride ends or you leave it. See Share Your Location. Does Live Tracking Work With No Cell Service? No. Positions only update when a phone has a connection. Offline maps keep the map and route on your screen, and riders without service show where they were last seen. Can I Use OnMyLead on an iPad or Android Phone? Yes. OnMyLead is in the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and on Google Play for Android phones and tablets. On a tablet the map fills the screen, see Use OnMyLead on a Tablet. You can also plan a ride on the website at onmylead.com, see Create a Ride on the Website. iPhone and Android riders can join the same ride, see each other on the map and chat together. How Many Waypoints Can I Add? Each rider can add up to 100 waypoints to a ride. See Waypoints and Planned Stops.

title: Import a GPX Route
summary: Bring in a track from Gaia, onX or any GPX file and use it as your ride's route. A Pro feature.
text: Already have the trail you want to ride as a track in another app? Export it as a GPX file and import it as your ride's route. Riders see it in Ride Mode just like a route drawn in OnMyLead. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Drawing a route on the map stays free: see Draw a Route. Import a File You need to be the ride's organizer or a co-organizer. Open the ride, tap the Map tab, and tap Build the Route (or Edit Route ). Tap Import GPX . Pick the GPX file. On iPhone it opens your Files, so save the file there first. Check the track on the map. The panel shows its miles and how many track points it has. Tap Save Route . If you're on the Free plan, tapping Import GPX shows what Pro includes instead of opening the file picker. What Gets Imported If the file has a track, the track is used. If it has no track, its route is used. If it has neither, its waypoints are joined in order. The track's name from the file is kept with the route. Very long tracks are simplified a little so they load and draw quickly on every rider's phone. Waypoints inside a GPX file aren't added as OnMyLead waypoints. To mark camp, fuel or a planned stop, see Waypoints and Planned Stops. Change an Imported Route An imported track is shown as it is, so you can't drag or add points to it. To use a different file, tap Clear , then Import GPX again. To draw your own instead, tap Clear and start tapping the map. Tapping a line on an imported route's map shows that trail's name and who can ride it. See Map Layers and Trails. GPX import works with Pro from either store: the App Store on iPhone and iPad, or Google Play on Android. If Your Pro Plan Ends A route you already imported stays on the ride. Importing a new GPX file needs Pro. On the Website Import GPX works the same way in the website's route builder. Pick the file from your computer. Troubleshooting "That file is not a GPX file." Go back to the other app, export the track as GPX (not KML or another format) and try again. "That GPX file has no track in it." The file doesn't have at least two points to draw. Export the track itself, not just a single waypoint.

title: Join a Ride
summary: Join with an invite link, a QR code or a code, or from Find. Learn what public and private rides show before and after you join.
text: Joining a ride is free, with no limit on how many rides you join. You need a free OnMyLead account. Join With a Link Tap the ride link someone sent you. If you have OnMyLead on your phone or tablet, the ride opens in the app. If not, it opens the ride's page on onmylead.com, with a button to get the app from the App Store or Google Play. Tap Join Ride . If you aren't signed in, the button says Sign In to Join . See Sign In. Join With a Code On the Rides tab, tap Join a Ride . Type the invite code, for example 7F3A9C21. Tap Open . On the ride page, tap Join Ride . Join With a QR Code Point your phone's camera at the ride's QR code and tap the link that appears. See QR Codes. Join From Find Public rides are listed on the Find tab. Open one and tap Join Ride . See Find a Ride. Join From a Group Invite When someone invites your riding group, you get a notification and the ride shows under Ride Invites on the Rides tab. Tap the ride. In the You're Invited card, tap Join Ride , or No Thanks to turn it down. You don't wait for approval when you're invited. If you say no thanks, you can still join later with the ride's link or code. On a ride where the organizer approves riders, you then ask to join like anyone else. Public and Private Rides Public rides can be found on the Find tab, and anyone can open their page. Private rides (marked Private, Invite Only ) never show in Find. You need the link, QR code or invite code to see one. Before you join either kind, the ride page shows the name, time, general area and details. After you join, you also see: The exact meeting point, and directions to it The organizer's instructions for joined riders The route and planned stops Who's going The ride chat After You Join The ride shows under Your Rides on the Rides tab. On the ride page you'll find Details , Map , Riders and Chat sections. When you get to the meeting spot, tap I'm Here and Ready to check in. See Check In. When the organizer starts the ride, tap Enter Ride Mode . See Ride Mode. If the ride is full, you go on the waitlist. If the organizer approves riders, you wait for them to say yes. See Approvals and the Waitlist. Leave a Ride Open the ride page and tap Riders . Tap Leave Ride . Or, on the Rides tab, swipe left on the ride and tap Leave (on onmylead.com, click Leave at the end of the ride's row). Your spot opens up for someone else. You can rejoin with the ride's link or code if there's room. If the ride is live, leaving also stops sharing your location with the group. You can't join a ride that has ended or been cancelled.

title: Send a Status or Quick Reply
summary: Tell the whole group what's happening with one tap, see who got it, and take it back if you tapped by mistake.
headings: When Another Rider Taps a Status
text: Ride Mode has big buttons so you can tell the group what's going on without typing. Every rider on the ride sees your tap, and you can see whose phone has it. Don't use your phone while you're moving. Pull over first, then tap. Quick Replies The four blue buttons send a short message to the group. They also show in the ride chat. On My Way Running Late Need a Minute All Good Status Buttons The grid below sets your status for the group: OK Stopped Need Fuel Mechanical Issue Flat Tire Stuck Lost Need Help EMERGENCY Need Help sends right away and shows in red for the group. EMERGENCY asks you to confirm first. See Emergencies and Safety. Send a Status In Ride Mode, tap a quick reply or a status button. A card appears above the buttons. It says Sending , then Sent to the Group . Watch the row of lights on the card, one per rider, with their first initial: A solid green light means that rider's app has it. A blue ring means a notification went to their phone, but their app hasn't shown it yet. An empty light means it hasn't reached them yet. Under the headline, the card spells it out, for example "Seen by Sam and Alex. 2 notified by push." or "All 5 riders got it." Tap ✕ to hide the card. It also goes away on its own after 10 minutes. Take It Back Tapped the wrong button? Tap Cancel on the card. The status or quick reply is taken back for everyone, the group is told to ignore it, and the notification they got is replaced with one saying you cancelled it. With No Signal If your tap can't go out within a few seconds, the card says Is Waiting for Signal . Your tap is saved on your phone and sends by itself when you get service, stamped with the time you tapped it. Tap Retry Now to try again right away, or Cancel to drop it. Clear Your Status While your status is anything other than OK, a card on your screen says Your Status and what you sent, with a reminder that the group sees it until you mark it resolved. Tap Resolved, I'm OK when you're sorted. This sends OK to the group. Mechanical Issue Mechanical Issue is for a machine that has broken down. Your spot shows on the map with an amber wrench, even if you aren't sharing your location. It uses where you were when you tapped. The leader, tail gunner and organizers hear it read aloud the moment you tap it, and it stays on their screen until you send another status. Your screen shows Mechanical Issue with Fixed, I'm OK . Tap it once you're rolling again. Mechanical Issue and EMERGENCY stay on screen even when you fold the bottom panel away. When Another Rider Taps a Status A card shows their name, their status and how long ago they tapped it, such as "Sam: Flat Tire, 2 min ago". Tap Navigate to get directions to them, or ✕ to hide it on your screen only. Calls drop off the list after 30 minutes. A Mechanical Issue stays until that rider sends another status. You get a notification on your phone. Need Help and EMERGENCY alerts are always on, even in quiet hours. Other statuses and quick replies follow your Rider Status setting. See Notification Settings. Regroup at My Location Organizers, co-organizers and leaders see a Regroup at My Location button above the quick replies. Tap it to set a regroup point where you are. Everyone on the ride sees a yellow pin on the map and a yellow banner, Regroup point set. Tap to navigate , and hears "Regroup point set." Tapping the banner opens directions to the regroup point. Setting a new regroup point replaces the old one. Leaders can also tap Regroup on a separation alert. See Ride Bubble.

title: Share a Family Link
summary: Send a read-only web link so family at home can see where you are, without the app or an account. It stops working when sharing ends.
text: A family link is a web link you can text to someone at home. They open it in any web browser, with no app and no account, and see your last known location and when sharing ends. It's free on every plan. Send a Family Link Tap the You tab. Under On the Trail , tap Share My Location . Turn on Family Link . Under For How Long , pick how long to share. If you pick Until I Turn It Off (Max 24 Hours) , tap Share to confirm. Your iPhone's share sheet opens with a message like "Follow my location until 5:30 PM" and the link. Pick Messages, or any app, and send it. You can pick riders under Who Can See You at the same time, or send just the family link. What They See The link opens a simple page with: Your ride name. Last update: when your phone last sent its location. Sharing ends: when the link stops working. Open in Maps: opens your last location in Google Maps. The page checks for a new location every 30 seconds. If your phone hasn't sent a location yet, it says No location received yet. The page shows your last update, not a guaranteed live position. With no service on the trail, Last update stays at the last time your phone got through. Tell your family what time you expect to be back, and what to do if they don't hear from you. Stop or Extend the Link The family link lasts exactly as long as the share it belongs to. Tap the You tab, then Share My Location . Find the card that says Includes a family link . Tap Add 1 Hour to keep it going, or Stop to end it now. Once the share ends, the link shows No Longer Shared and This location link has ended. Your location can't be seen from it again. Anyone who has the link can see your location until the share ends, so only send it to people you trust.

title: Use Your Riding Group's Chat
summary: Talk with your whole riding group between rides, link a message to a ride, mute a busy group and clear messages.
text: Every riding group has its own chat: a group text for everyone in the group. Use it to plan the next ride or talk about the last one. It's separate from ride chat, which is for the riders on one ride. Group chat is free for everyone in the group. Only the riders in the group can read it or post in it. Open the Chat Tap the Groups tab. Tap the newest message under a group, or open the group and tap Group Chat . Groups with messages you haven't read show a red count. Send a Message Type in the box at the bottom. Tap the send button. Your message shows Sending , then Sent . If it can't go through, for example with no signal, it shows Not Sent . Tap Retry to send it again, or Remove to drop it. Messages can be up to 500 characters. If you send a lot of messages in a row, the app asks you to wait a minute. Talk About a Ride You can tie a message to one of your rides, so everyone knows which ride you mean. Tap About a Ride above the message box. Under Which Ride Is This About? , pick the ride. Type your message and send it. The list shows rides you've joined that are happening now, coming up, or ended in the last 30 days. To send without a ride, tap the ride's name above the message box to remove it. Rides the group has talked about show in a strip at the top of the chat. Tap a ride to see only the talk about it, and tap Open the Ride to go to its page. Tap All Talk to see every message again. Mute a Group Tap Mute at the top of the chat to stop notifications from that group. Tap Unmute to turn them back on. To turn off notifications for all your groups' chats, switch off Riding Group Chat in Notification Settings. Clear a Message Your own message: press and hold it, then confirm Clear . It disappears for everyone, and this can't be undone. If you run the group: press and hold anyone's message and tap Clear . Report or Block a Rider Press and hold someone else's message, then tap Report Rider or Block Rider . Messages from riders you've blocked aren't shown to you. See Report and Block.

title: Your Free 30-Day Pro Trial
summary: Every new account gets 30 days of OnMyLead Pro with no payment, and it never turns into a paid subscription on its own.
headings: See How Many Days Are Left
text: When you make a new OnMyLead account, you get 30 days of OnMyLead Pro for free. It starts on its own. There's nothing to sign up for and no payment details to enter. You're never charged when the trial ends. It does not turn into a paid subscription. Your account simply moves to Free unless you choose to subscribe. See How Many Days Are Left On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Your Plan shows Pro Trial with the days remaining, the date it ends, and a row of 30 marks that fills in as the days go by. The trial is the same on Android. It belongs to your account, not your phone, so it shows the same days left on every device you sign in to. Trial Reminders OnMyLead reminds you a week, 3 days and a day before your trial ends, and again when it ends. To turn off the notifications, switch off Pro Trial Reminders in Notification Settings. The same reminders come by email too. Switch off Email Me Too to stop the emails. When the Trial Ends Your account moves to Free. Nothing you made during the trial is deleted: Your rides, routes, groups and downloaded maps stay yours. New Pro actions, like downloading another map area or importing a GPX file, need Pro again. Free accounts create one ride a month. Rides you created earlier in the same month, during the trial, count toward that month. See Free and Pro for exactly what changes. Keep Pro After the Trial On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Keep Pro After the Trial . Choose Annual or Monthly . Tap the Subscribe for button under the plans and confirm with Apple. Apple charges you when you confirm, and your paid subscription starts right away. See Subscribe to Pro. Good to Know Each account gets one trial. The trial is part of OnMyLead, not an Apple free trial, so it doesn't show in your Apple subscriptions.

title: Your Ride Name and Profile
summary: Pick the ride name other riders see on the map, the rider list and in chat, and choose whether to show your Apple, Google or Facebook profile.
headings: Pick or Change Your Ride Name
Where Your Name Comes From at First
Show Your Apple, Google or Facebook Profile
text: Your ride name is how the group knows you. It shows on the group map, the rider list and in ride chat. A nickname works fine. Pick or Change Your Ride Name Go to the You tab and tap your name at the top. If you haven't picked one yet, it says Pick Your Ride Name . You can also tap Pick Your Ride Name on the Rides tab. Type your name in Ride Name . Check the preview at the top. It shows your pin on the map and a chat line, the way the group sees you. Tap Save Name . The button changes to Name Saved . Until you pick a name, other riders see you as Rider. Keep it to 24 characters or fewer so it fits on the map. Extra spaces are tidied up when you save. Where Your Name Comes From at First If you created your account with your name, or signed in with Apple, Google or Facebook, your ride name may already be filled in from that. You can change it any time. Show Your Apple, Google or Facebook Profile If you signed in with Apple, Google or Facebook, you can let the riders you ride with see that account's name and photo. It helps people recognize who joined. Go to the You tab. Under Account , find Show My Google Profile (or Show My Apple Profile or Show My Facebook Profile , depending on how you signed in). Turn the switch on. When it's on, your photo replaces your initial, and a line like "Your Name on Google" shows under your ride name in a ride's rider list and in your riding groups. When it's off, nobody else sees it. It's off until you turn it on. Who Can See It Only riders who have been on a ride with you or share a riding group with you. Never strangers browsing public rides. Never someone you've blocked, or who has blocked you. The name and photo come from the account you signed in with, and the app keeps them up to date each time you open the You tab. You can only turn the setting on or off. If you signed in with email only, this setting doesn't appear. Your Email Under Account on the You tab, Email shows the email on your account. Only you see it.

title: Contact Us
summary: Send the OnMyLead team a message from the app or the website about a problem, an idea, billing, your account or safety.
headings: Send a Message From the App
Send a Message From the Website
text: Questions, problems or ideas for OnMyLead go straight to the team at RUS Offroad. A real person reads every message. OnMyLead is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 911 or your local emergency number first. Send a Message From the App Go to the You tab. Under Help , tap Contact Us . Under What's It About? , pick a topic: Something Isn't Working Feature Request Billing and Pro Account and Sign-In Safety or a Rider General Feedback Something Else Check Your Name (optional) and Your Email . If you're signed in, they're filled in for you. Write Your Message . The hint under the box suggests what to include for your topic. Tap Send Message . You'll see Message Sent . We reply to the email you gave, usually within a day. Send a Message From the Website Go to onmylead.com/contact. The same form works there, and you don't need to sign in. Email Us You can also email support@rusoffroad.com. Tips for a Quick Answer Something Isn't Working : tell us what you tapped, what happened and what you expected. The ride name helps if it's about a ride. Billing and Pro : purchases are billed by Apple, and refunds go through reportaproblem.apple.com. We're still glad to help. On Android, the hint says purchases are billed by Google Play, with refunds through your Google Play order history. Account and Sign-In : if you sign in with a different email than the one on the form, tell us which. Safety or a Rider : to report a rider, you can also press and hold their message in a ride. See Report or Block a Rider. Help and Support Page Under Help on the You tab, Help and Support has short answers to common questions about joining rides, location and battery, Pro, blocking and deleting your account. In the Android app, those answers give the Android steps where they differ, such as allowing location While Using the App .

title: Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride
summary: Change your ride's route and stops, call a ride off so riders hear about it, or delete it for good.
text: Plans change. As the organizer you can update the route and stops, cancel the ride so everyone knows it's off, or delete it entirely. What You Can Change On your ride page, you can change: The route. Open the Map section and tap Edit Route (or Build the Route if there isn't one yet, or Map a Route Anyway on a freeride). See Build a Route. Planned stops. In the Map section, tap Add a Planned Stop . See Waypoints and Planned Stops. Who leads and who rides at the rear. See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner. The ride's name, day, meeting time and meeting point can't be changed after the ride is created. To move a ride, tap Copy This Ride on its page to start a new one with the same details and route, pick the new day, then cancel the old one. The copy counts as a new ride toward your monthly allowance on Free. Cancel a Ride Cancel when the ride is off but you want everyone to see that it was called off. The ride stays in their list as Cancelled. Open the ride page. In the You're Organizing card on Details , tap Cancel Ride . Read the message. It tells you how many riders will hear about it. Tap Cancel Ride to confirm, or Keep Ride to go back. Everyone who joined, asked to join or is on the waitlist gets a notification and an email saying the ride is cancelled. Cancelling can't be undone. You can cancel a ride that hasn't started yet or one that's live. A ride that has already ended can't be cancelled. Delete a Ride Delete removes the ride for everyone, along with its chat and route. Only the ride's organizer can delete it. Open the ride page. In the You're Organizing card, tap Delete Ride . Tap Delete Ride to confirm. If the ride hadn't ended yet, everyone on it gets a notification and an email saying it's cancelled. Deleting can't be undone. You can also delete a ride from the Rides tab. Swipe left on the ride under Your Rides or Past Rides and tap Delete . On onmylead.com there's nothing to swipe: each ride on the Rides page has its own button at the end of the row. Click the trash can ( Delete ) on a ride you organize, then confirm. On a ride someone else organizes the button is Leave (or Decline for an invite). Cancel or Delete: Which One? Cancel keeps the ride in everyone's list, marked Cancelled. Delete removes it, its chat and its route for everyone. Either way, riders on an upcoming ride are told it's off. Cancelling or deleting doesn't give back a ride on a Free account. A ride counts toward the month you created it. See Free and Pro.

title: Follow a Ride Leader
summary: Follow the riders who organize and lead your favorite rides and get a notification when they post a new public ride.
text: Liked a ride? Follow the rider who organized or led it, and you'll hear when they post their next public ride. Following is free. Follow a Leader Open the ride's page. If you've joined the ride, go to Riders . Find the organizer or ride leader. Each one is labeled Organizer or Ride Leader . Tap Follow . The button changes to Following . To stop, tap Following on a ride page, or use Unfollow on the Groups tab (see below). You can't follow yourself, so your own name doesn't get a Follow button. What You Get A notification when a leader you follow posts a new public ride. Private and unlisted rides are never announced to followers. On the Groups tab, under Leaders You Follow , a list of the leaders you follow, and under Their Upcoming Rides , their upcoming public rides. To turn these notifications off, switch off Leaders You Follow in Notification Settings. Unfollow a Leader Tap the Groups tab. Under Leaders You Follow , tap Unfollow next to the leader. Who Sees a Follow Only you and the leader can see that you follow them. If riders follow you, the Groups tab shows how many.

title: Invite Riders
summary: Send your ride by text, email or any app, copy its link, show a QR code, or invite a whole riding group in one tap.
text: Every ride has a link, an invite code and a QR code. Send any of them and your friends can open the ride and join. Find the Invite Card Right after you create a ride, its page opens with the invite card at the top. Later, open the ride page and tap Riders to find the Invite Riders card. Anyone on a ride can share it, not just the organizer. On a public ride, anyone who can see the ride page can share it. On a private ride, only riders who have joined see the invite card. Send the Invite On the invite card, tap: Share Invite to send it with any app on your phone Text to open a new text message Email to open a new email Copy Link to copy the ride's link, then paste it anywhere The message includes the ride name, the link and the invite code. When your friend taps the link, the ride opens in OnMyLead if they have it, or on onmylead.com with a button to get the app. On Android, ride and riding group links open straight in the OnMyLead app once it's installed. Share the Code The Invite Code is shown in big letters on the card. Friends can type it on the Rides tab under Join a Ride . See Join a Ride. Show a QR Code Tap Show QR Code (or the small QR code) to show it full screen, so riders at the trailhead can scan it off your phone. See QR Codes. Invite a Riding Group Organizers can invite everyone in a riding group at once. Each rider gets a notification and sees the ride on their Rides tab, and they join with one tap. From the ride page: Open the ride page and tap Riders . On the invite card, under Invite a Group , tap Invite All next to the group. From the group: On the Groups tab, open the group. Tap Invite to a Ride . Tap the ride. It lists the upcoming rides you organize. You can also pick groups under Invite a Group when you create the ride. See Create a Ride. Invited riders skip approval, even on a ride where you approve riders. Saving a riding group is a Pro feature, but inviting a group you're already in to your ride is not. See Riding Groups and Free and Pro. Public or Private? Public rides can also be found by riders near you or in your state on the Find tab. Private rides are only found by people you send the link, QR code or code to. Anyone holding them can join, so share them only with people you want on the ride.

title: Keep the Group Together with Ride Bubble
summary: Ride Bubble watches for riders who drop back, run ahead or stop moving, and warns the leader and tail gunner before anyone gets lost.
headings: What the Leader and Tail Gunner See
text: Ride Bubble keeps an eye on the gaps in the group while Ride Mode is open. When a rider gets too far from everyone else, stops while the group keeps moving, or goes quiet, Ride Bubble flags them. It's free on every plan. How It Decides Each rider is measured against the nearest other rider, not just the leader. That way a rider who has run far ahead counts too, and the tail gunner at the back is measured against the last rider rather than the whole pack. A rider turns yellow or red when: They're too far from the nearest rider. The distances depend on the ride's Ride Bubble setting (below). They've stopped while at least half the group is moving. Yellow after 2 minutes stopped, red after 5 minutes. Their phone has gone quiet. No update for 5 minutes turns a rider red, with a message like "No update from Sam for 6 minutes. Showing last known location." Only riders who are sharing their location are part of Ride Bubble. A rider who isn't sharing can't be measured. Ride Bubble Settings The organizer picks the setting when creating the ride, under Add Route, Difficulty and More , in Ride Bubble . Setting Yellow when the nearest rider is more than Red when the nearest rider is more than --- --- --- Standard 0.5 miles 1.5 miles Tight Trail 0.1 miles 0.25 miles Desert 0.75 miles 2 miles Highway 1 mile 3 miles The stopped and no-update times are the same for every setting. What Everyone Sees A yellow or red ring around a rider's dot on the map. At the top of Ride Mode, Together in green, or the number of red riders, such as 2 Separated , in red. Tap it to see every rider and when they last updated. What the Leader and Tail Gunner See The ride's leader, tail gunner, organizer and co-organizers also get: An alert card for each yellow or red rider, such as "Mike is 1.7 miles behind the group. Last moving 4 minutes ago." Tap Navigate for directions to them. Leaders and organizers can also tap Regroup to set a regroup point at their location. A spoken alert and a buzz the moment a rider turns red, so you don't have to look down. The alert cards hide when the bottom panel is folded. Tap Buttons ▲ to open the panel and see them. Spoken alerts pause while your own phone has no service. When you lose signal everyone looks quiet, and that's your signal dropping, not theirs. Tips Ask everyone to share their location for the whole ride so Ride Bubble can see them. See Share Your Location. Give someone the tail gunner role so the back of the group is covered. See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner.

title: Notification Settings
summary: Choose which ride, chat, group and account notifications you get, set a ride reminder and quiet hours. Help and EMERGENCY alerts always come through.
headings: What You Can Turn On or Off
text: You decide what OnMyLead tells you about. Every change saves as soon as you make it, and your choices apply on any device you sign in on. Open Notification Settings Go to the You tab. Under Settings , tap Notifications . The line under it sums up your settings, like Everything on or 2 turned off . Always On: Help and EMERGENCY When someone in your group taps Need Help or EMERGENCY , you're always told, even during quiet hours. This can't be turned off. What You Can Turn On or Off Everything below starts on. On the Trail Rider Status : status buttons and quick replies from Ride Mode, like On My Way , Need Fuel and Flat Tire , and when a rider cancels one. Announcements : what the organizer tells the whole group. Ride Chat Group Chat : messages and quick replies from your group. Messages to the Leader : leader-only messages, when you're leading. Show Message Text : turn this off to keep messages off your lock screen. You'll see who wrote, not what. Before the Ride Ride Changes : a ride starts, is cancelled, or gets a new time or meeting spot, or you get a spot or a role. New Riders : someone joins or asks to join a ride you organize. Email When a Ride Is Cancelled : an email as well as the notification if a ride you joined is cancelled or removed. Your Riding Groups Ride Invites : someone invites you, or a group you're in, to a ride. Riding Group Chat : new messages in your riding groups' chats. To mute just one group, do it from that group's chat. See Group Chat. Leaders You Follow : a leader you follow posts a new public ride. Your Account Pro Trial Reminders : a week, 3 days and a day before your Pro Trial ends, and when it does. Email Me Too : the same Pro Trial reminders by email. Tapping a Notification Tapping a notification takes you straight to what it's about, whether OnMyLead was open, in the background or closed: A status tap like Need Help , a quick reply, or a ride going live opens Ride Mode for that ride. A ride chat message opens the ride's Chat . A riding group message opens that group's chat. Ride changes, new riders, invites and reminders open the ride. Ride Reminder Get a heads-up before each ride you've joined, with the meeting spot. Under Ride reminder , pick Off , 30 Min , 1 Hour , 2 Hours or Day Before . It starts at 1 Hour . Quiet Hours Under Quiet hours , turn on Silence Overnight . Use the minus and plus buttons under From and Until to set the times. Each tap moves the time by half an hour. During quiet hours everything is held except help alerts. Until you change them, quiet hours run from 10 PM to 6 AM. If Notifications Aren't Arriving If you see Notifications Are Off for OnMyLead , your iPhone is blocking them. Tap Open iPhone Settings and turn on Allow Notifications . On Android, the button is Open Settings . Android also sorts OnMyLead's notifications into three categories you can tune in Settings Apps OnMyLead Notifications : Rider Alerts (Need Help, EMERGENCY and other status taps, shown at the highest priority), Ride Chat (ride and group chat) and Ride Updates (ride changes, new riders, invites, reminders and account notices). If you see Let OnMyLead Send Notifications , tap Turn On Notifications and allow them. While OnMyLead is open, new ride chat messages pop up inside the app instead of as a banner. On the Website You can change these settings at onmylead.com too. Notifications themselves come to the app on your phone or tablet.

title: Subscribe to OnMyLead Pro
summary: Choose the monthly or annual plan and subscribe to OnMyLead Pro in the app, billed through your Apple Account or Google Play.
headings: Already Have Pro From the Other Store?
text: OnMyLead Pro adds unlimited rides, offline maps, GPX import, saved riding groups and more. See Free and Pro for the full list. Prices Plan US Price --- --- Monthly $4.99 a month Annual $29.99 a year, about $2.50 a month. Saves about 50% compared with paying monthly. Outside the US, the app shows the price in your local currency. Subscribe On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Upgrade to Pro . During your free trial, this button says Keep Pro After the Trial . Choose Annual (marked Best Value ) or Monthly . Tap the Subscribe for button under the plans, for example Subscribe for $29.99 a Year . Confirm the purchase in Apple's window. On Android, step 5 is Google Play's window instead, and the payment goes to your Google Play account. When it's done, the app says You’re on OnMyLead Pro. Thanks for riding with us. and your plan shows Pro . You can also reach the Pro screen by tapping See OnMyLead Pro on any Pro prompt, or Unlimited With Pro on the Create a Ride screen. You can subscribe in the OnMyLead app only, on iPhone, iPad or Android. The website can't sell subscriptions, but Pro you buy in the app also works when you use OnMyLead on the website. Already Have Pro From the Other Store? Pro belongs to your OnMyLead account, so a subscription from the App Store works on Android and one from Google Play works on iPhone and iPad. If you already pay for Pro through one store, the Pro screen on a device that uses the other store says so instead of showing the plans, so you aren't charged twice. To move your subscription to the other store, cancel it in the store you pay now and subscribe on the other device after it ends. Billing Payment is charged to your Apple Account when you confirm the purchase. The subscription renews automatically unless you turn it off at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Renewal is charged within the 24 hours before the period ends. You can manage or cancel anytime in your Apple Account settings. See Manage or Cancel Your Subscription. On Android, payment is charged to your Google Play account when you confirm. The subscription renews automatically at the end of each period until you cancel it in Google Play, and Pro stays on until the end of the period you paid for. The free Pro Trial for new accounts is separate. It needs no payment and never turns into a paid subscription on its own. The Pro screen links to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy . If Something Goes Wrong "Waiting on Apple to approve the purchase." This happens with Ask to Buy or when your bank needs to check the payment. Once it's approved, Pro starts on its own. "Waiting on Google Play to approve the purchase." This happens when you pay with a method Google confirms later, such as cash at a store. Pro starts on its own once the payment goes through. "The purchase didn’t go through. You weren’t charged." Check your connection and try again. Your plan still says Free after buying. Make sure you have signal, then close and reopen the app. If it still says Free, tap Restore Purchases . See Restore Purchases.
