title: Waypoints and Planned Stops
summary: Mark camp, fuel, water or a hazard on a ride's map, and let the leader plan numbered stops for the whole group.
text: Waypoints are named spots you drop on a ride's map: camp, fuel, water, a viewpoint, a hazard or parking. Your own waypoints are only for you. The ride's leader can also share waypoints with everyone on the ride, and plan numbered stops the whole group will make. Waypoints are never public. Shared ones and planned stops show only to riders on that ride. Who Sees What Your waypoints : only you see them, unless you can share (below). Shared waypoints : the leader or an organizer can share a waypoint with everyone on the ride. Planned stops : always shared. Every rider sees them numbered on the map, in order. The leader is the rider with the Leader role, or the organizer when nobody has it. See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner. You need to have joined the ride to add or see its waypoints. Add a Waypoint Open the ride and tap the Map tab. Under Waypoints , tap Add a Waypoint (or Open Waypoints Map if there are some already). Press and hold the map where you want it (click it on onmylead.com). To mark where you're standing, tap Add at My Location instead. Pick what it is: Spot , Camp , Fuel , Water , Viewpoint , Hazard or Parking . The name fills in for you. Change the Name if you like, and add a Note (Optional) . If you're the leader or an organizer, choose who it's for under What It Is (see below). Tap Save Waypoint . In Ride Mode, tap Add Waypoint to drop one where you are, or press and hold the map. See Ride Mode. Names can be up to 60 characters and notes up to 280. Sharing a Waypoint (Leader and Organizers) When the leader or an organizer adds a waypoint, they choose: Planned Stop : the whole ride stops here. Numbered on every rider's map. Everyone on the Ride : shows on every rider's map. Just Me : only you see it. New waypoints from the leader or an organizer start as Everyone on the Ride , and you can switch to Just Me . Plan the Ride's Stops Planned stops tell everyone where the group will stop for fuel, lunch or camp, and in what order. Open the ride and tap the Map tab. Under Planned Stops , tap Add a Planned Stop . Press and hold the map where the group will stop. Pick what it is and give it a name. Add a Planned Time (Optional) , like "12:30 pm". Tap Save Planned Stop . Stops are numbered in the order you add them. To change the order: Tap a planned stop on the map or in the list. Tap Move Earlier or Move Later . The leader or an organizer can edit any planned stop on the ride, even ones someone else added, so the plan carries on if the leader changes. View, Navigate, Edit or Remove Tap a waypoint on the map or in the list to open it. You'll see its type, who it's from, the note and its coordinates. Navigate : get directions in your maps app. See Directions. Edit : change it. You can edit your own waypoints. The leader or an organizer can also edit planned stops. Remove : take it off the map. You can remove your own. The leader or an organizer can also remove shared ones. When a shared waypoint is removed, everyone stops seeing it. On the Website The waypoints map works on onmylead.com too. Click the map to drop a waypoint, and click a waypoint to open it. On a tablet held sideways, the waypoint list sits beside the map; swipe it up or tap Hide to fold it. No Signal The waypoints you can see are saved on your phone, so they stay on the map without signal. The panel shows Saved on This Phone when that's what you're seeing. Limits Each rider can add up to 100 waypoints on a ride. If you reach that, remove one to add another. Waypoints are different from the numbered points you tap when drawing a route. Route points shape the line; waypoints mark places along the way.

title: What Other Riders Can See
summary: Your location is never public. See what strangers, riders on your ride and family links can see, and how OnMyLead's server enforces it.
text: OnMyLead is built so your location is never public. You choose who sees it and for how long, and sharing always ends. These rules are enforced by OnMyLead's server, not just hidden in the app. Before You Join a Ride Anyone can see a ride's public page: its name, time, description and details such as difficulty and vehicles. What they don't get: The exact meeting point. Public listings and the ride map show a meeting area rounded to about a mile. The ride page says Shown after you join , or Near and the area's name. The route, the meeting instructions and the roster. Only riders who have joined the ride get these. The exact meeting point and the route are stored separately from the public ride, and the server only hands them to riders on the ride. Riders on Your Ride Once you've joined a ride, the other riders on it can see: Your ride name. If you turned on Show My Google (or Apple or Facebook) Profile , they also see that account's name and photo. See Your Ride Name and Profile. That you're on the ride, your role, and whether you've checked in. Your messages in the ride chat, except leader-only messages, which only you and the leader can read. Your status taps and quick replies from Ride Mode. A status tap carries your phone's location at the moment you tapped it. Your live location, but only while you're sharing with the ride. Your Live Location The server only lets someone read your location while all of these are true: You have turned sharing on. Your share hasn't run out or been stopped. They are someone your share covers: a rider on that ride, a rider you picked, or someone with your family link. For ride sharing, the ride is still going and you're still on it. When the ride ends, every ride share on it stops at once. When you leave a ride, your share for it stops. See Share Your Location. Your Ride Track While you share with a ride, your phone keeps a track of where you rode for your ride summary. Only you can see your own track. The group summary shows totals only, never anyone's route. Waypoints Waypoints you drop are only yours, unless you're the ride's leader and choose to share one with the ride. See Waypoints and Planned Stops. Family Links Anyone with your family link can see your last location until that share ends. See Share a Family Link. Blocked Riders When you block a rider, nothing tells them, and they can't see who has blocked them. See Report or Block a Rider. Your Data OnMyLead doesn't sell your data or use it for advertising. It shares data only with the services that run the app, such as Apple for notifications and purchases on iPhone. For the full list, read the Privacy Policy at onmylead.com/privacy. On Android, Google delivers notifications (Firebase Cloud Messaging), handles purchases (Google Play) and draws the map (Google Maps). You can delete your account and its data at any time. See Delete Your Account.

title: Check Your Fuel Range for a Ride
summary: See if your machine's tank covers the ride's miles, using the thirds rule, before you leave and in Ride Mode.
headings: Where the Ride's Miles Come From
text: Trail miles burn more fuel than you think. OnMyLead compares a ride's miles with your machine's range from your garage and tells you, in plain words, whether you have enough. How Range Is Worked Out Your range is your fuel (tank plus any extra fuel you carry) times your miles per gallon. The check uses the thirds rule: a third out, a third back and a third in reserve. Enough Range : the ride is within two thirds of your full range, so you keep a reserve. Range Is Tight : the ride eats into your reserve. Bring extra fuel or plan a fill-up. Not Enough Range : the ride is longer than your full range. The check says about how many miles short you are. When you have enough, it also says roughly how much fuel you'll have left at the end. Set Up Your Machine The check needs your machine's tank size and mileage. Open your machine in the Garage and edit it. Under Fuel and Mileage , enter Tank (gal) . If you carry spare fuel, enter Extra Fuel (gal) . Enter Miles per Gallon . Use your real-world trail mpg, not the sticker number. Save. Your machine's page then shows its Full Range , Safe Turnaround and Safe Trip miles. See Your Garage. Where the Ride's Miles Come From If the ride has a mapped route, its miles come from the route. See Draw a Route. If not, the organizer can enter Route Length (Miles) when creating the ride, under Add Route, Difficulty and More . A ride with neither has no miles to check against. Check Before the Ride Join the ride, open it and tap the Details tab. Find the fuel card. Until there's a result, it's called Your Machine . Under Bringing , pick the machine you're taking, or None / Riding Along . Read the result: Enough Range , Range Is Tight or Not Enough Range , with one line of advice. If you have only one machine with a tank size and mpg, it's checked until you pick one. You can change your machine while the ride is scheduled or live. If the card says to add tank size and mpg, tap Edit Machine . If your garage is empty, tap Add Your Machine to the Garage . In Ride Mode When the ride has a mapped route, Ride Mode shows your range check with the route progress, colored green, yellow or red. It uses the route's length and the machine you picked for the ride. See Ride Mode. Running low on the trail? Use the Need Fuel status button to let the group know. See Status Buttons. Good to Know The check is worked out for you from your own garage. It's a planning guide, not a gauge. Hills, sand, mud, load and speed all change real fuel use. The Trip Planner has a fuel check too. See Trip Planner.

title: Manage or Cancel Your Subscription
summary: Change between monthly and annual or cancel OnMyLead Pro in your Apple Account settings, and see what happens when Pro ends.
headings: Cancel or Change Your Plan in the App
Cancel or Change It on Android
Cancel or Change It in iPhone Settings
text: OnMyLead Pro is billed by Apple, so you change or cancel it in your Apple Account settings. The app takes you straight there. Cancel or Change Your Plan in the App On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Manage Subscription . Apple's subscription screen opens. Choose a different plan, or cancel your subscription. If you pay for Pro, the Pro screen also has a Manage Subscription button where the plans usually are. Cancel or Change It on Android On Android, Pro is billed by Google Play. Manage Subscription opens Google Play's subscription page for OnMyLead, where you can change plans or cancel. You can also do it in the Play Store app: tap your profile picture, then Payments & Subscriptions Subscriptions OnMyLead . If you bought Pro on a different kind of device (on an iPhone while you're on Android, or the other way round), Manage Subscription tells you which store bills it and opens that store's subscription page. Cancel it there. Cancel or Change It in iPhone Settings Open the Settings app on your iPhone. Tap your name at the top. Tap Subscriptions . Tap OnMyLead , then choose a plan or cancel. To avoid being charged for the next period, cancel at least 24 hours before your current period ends. The subscription renews automatically until you turn it off. Check When It Renews On the Subscription screen, Your Plan shows Pro and the date it renews or ends. What Happens When Pro Ends When a subscription you cancelled reaches the end of the period you paid for, your account moves to Free. Nothing is deleted: Rides: every ride you created stays. Free accounts create one new ride a month. Routes: routes you already imported from GPX stay and stay editable. Importing a new GPX file needs Pro. Offline maps: maps already on your phone keep working. Downloading new map areas needs Pro. Riding groups: your groups stay, with their chats, and you can still invite them to your rides. Creating a group or adding and removing riders needs Pro. Polls: polls already sent can still be voted on. Creating a new poll needs Pro. Ride history: Home shows your last 5 past rides. The rest are saved, and show again if you upgrade. Trips: your trips stay. Free plans one active trip at a time. See Free and Pro for the full comparison. Good to Know Deleting your OnMyLead account does not cancel the Apple subscription. Cancel it in your Apple subscriptions too, so you aren't billed again. See Delete Your Account. If your plan says Complimentary Pro , it was given to you by OnMyLead and isn't billed by Apple, so there's nothing to cancel. Deleting your OnMyLead account doesn't cancel a Google Play subscription either. Cancel it in Google Play too. On Android, Your Plan also says which store bills your Pro. Subscriptions can only be managed in the app on your phone or tablet. On the website, the Subscription screen says so.

title: Organizer Controls
summary: Everything you can do as a ride's organizer, from starting Ride Mode and approving riders to ending the ride for everyone.
text: When you create a ride, you're its organizer. You're also its leader until you hand that job to someone else. Here's what you can do from your ride page. Before the Ride Invite riders. Share the link, code or QR code, or invite a whole riding group. See Invite Riders. Approve requests. If riders asked to join, the Riders section shows a red count and a Waiting for You list with Approve and Decline . See Approvals and the Waitlist. Build or edit the route and add planned stops in the Map section. See Build a Route. Pick a leader and a tail gunner from the roster in Riders . See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner. Post announcements in the ride chat. Your latest announcement is pinned near the top of the ride page for everyone on the ride. See Ride Chat. You get a notification when someone joins or asks to join a ride you organize. You can turn these off in Notification Settings. Start the Ride Open the ride page. Tap Start Ride Mode . The ride goes live, riders on it get a notification that it started, and Ride Mode opens for you. Everyone else on the ride sees Enter Ride Mode on the ride page, and a banner on their Rides tab. See Ride Mode. End the Ride When everyone is off the trail: Open the ride page. In the You're Organizing card on Details , tap End Ride for Everyone . Ending the ride stops everyone's location sharing for this ride. Riders then see their ride summary on the ride page. See Ride Summary and Ride Again. A live ride doesn't end by itself. Remember to tap End Ride for Everyone when you're done, so location sharing for the ride stops. Hand Off the Whole Ride If you can't make it, give the ride to another rider who has joined. Open Riders , tap their name and tap Give Them the Ride . They become the organizer and leader, and you stay on the ride as a rider. You can't undo this yourself. See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner. Call It Off Use Cancel Ride or Delete Ride in the You're Organizing card. See Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride. Run It Again Tap Copy This Ride (or Ride Again after it ends) to start a new ride with the same details and route. See Ride Summary and Ride Again. As the organizer you can't leave your own ride. Hand it to another rider first if you need to step away.

title: QR Codes
summary: Show your ride's QR code so riders can scan it at the trailhead, share it as a picture, or scan one to join a ride.
headings: Share the QR Code as a Picture
Scan a QR Code to Join
text: Every ride has its own QR code. It's the quickest way to get riders on your ride at the trailhead: they point their camera at your screen and they're in. Show Your Ride's QR Code Open the ride page. Right after creating a ride, the invite card is at the top. Later, tap Riders to find it. Tap Show QR Code , or tap the small QR code on the card. The QR code opens full screen with the ride name and the invite code under it ( Or Enter Code ), so riders can type the code if their camera won't scan. Tap Done to close it. Share the QR Code as a Picture Show the QR code full screen. Tap Share QR Code . Pick how to send it: text, email or any app. It sends a picture of the QR code card along with the ride link. You can print it or post it for a club ride. Scan a QR Code to Join Open your phone's Camera and point it at the QR code. Tap the link that appears. If you have OnMyLead, you go straight to the ride. If not, the ride's page opens on onmylead.com with a button to get the app. Tap Join Ride . See Join a Ride. Opened a ride link on your computer? The ride's web page shows its QR code. Scan it with your phone to open the ride there. The QR code holds only the ride's link and invite code. It doesn't show the meeting point. On a private ride, anyone who scans it can join, so share it with care.

title: Report or Block a Rider
summary: Report a rider or a ride to the OnMyLead team, and block a rider to hide their chat messages. Nobody is told who reported or blocked them.
text: If a rider or a ride isn't right, report it to the OnMyLead team. If you'd rather not hear from a rider, block them. Neither one tells the other person it was you. If anyone is in danger, call 911 first. Report a Rider Open the ride and tap Riders . In the Going list, tap the rider. Tap Report Rider . Under What's Wrong , pick Harassment , Unsafe Riding , Spam or Scam , Fake Account or Something Else . Add details under Anything Else (Optional) if you like. Tap Send Report . You can also press and hold one of the rider's messages in ride chat or group chat, then tap Report Rider . Report a Ride Open the ride's page. Scroll to the bottom and tap Report Ride . Under What's Wrong , pick Unsafe Plan , Spam or Scam , Offensive Content or Something Else . Add details if you like, then tap Send Report . Reports go to the OnMyLead team, not to the rider or the organizer. OnMyLead looks at every report, and the person reported isn't told who sent it. Block a Rider Blocking hides a rider's chat from you. Open the ride and tap Riders . In the Going list, tap the rider. Tap Block Rider . Tap Block to confirm. You can also block from: Ride chat or group chat: press and hold their message, then tap Block Rider . A report: tap Block This Rider , or Also Block This Rider after you send it. What Blocking Does You don't see their messages or polls in ride chat or group chat. You don't get chat notifications or pop-ups from them. They aren't told, and they can't see that you blocked them. What Blocking Doesn't Do Announcements and Ride Mode quick replies from them still show, because they carry the plan and safety of a ride you're both on. Their Need Help and EMERGENCY alerts always come through. It doesn't remove them from a ride or stop them seeing you on a ride you're both on. If you're worried about your safety on a ride, leave the ride or stop sharing your location. See Share Your Location. Unblock a Rider Tap the You tab. Under Settings , tap Blocked Riders . Tap Unblock next to the rider. You can also tap the rider in a ride's Going list and tap Unblock Rider .

title: Use OnMyLead on a Tablet
summary: On an iPad or Android tablet the map fills the screen, with the riders, the ride details and your buttons beside it.
headings: Draw a Route and Add Waypoints
text: OnMyLead works the same on a tablet as on a phone, with the same account, rides and Pro plan. A tablet just gets layouts made for the bigger screen: the map fills it, and the riders, the ride details and your buttons sit beside the map instead of on top of it. Turn It Either Way Hold the tablet upright or sideways; every screen works both ways. Phones stay upright. You can also run OnMyLead next to another app (Split View or Slide Over on an iPad, split screen on Android). The layout follows the size of the window: in a narrow window you get the phone layout, and it switches back as the window grows. Getting Around On a tablet, Rides , Find , Groups and You run down the left edge of the screen instead of along the bottom. On Rides , with the tablet sideways, Create a Ride , Join a Ride and Find a Ride stay on the left and your rides are listed beside them. Ride Mode on a Tablet The live map fills the screen. Riders sit in a list on the left with how fresh each rider's location is. Tap the arrow beside a rider to get directions to them. Tap Hide , or swipe the list to the left, to see more map; tap Show Riders to bring it back. The list starts open with the tablet sideways and folded with it upright. Your buttons (the route strip, quick replies and status buttons) sit in a panel on the right. Swipe it down or tap Hide to fold it, just like on a phone. Mechanical Issue and EMERGENCY always stay on screen. Directions and Add Waypoint sit just above the buttons panel. The ride name, your sharing timer and any announcement stay at the top of the left side. The Ride Page Once you've joined a ride, the ride and its details stay on the left, and Map , Riders and Chat open on the right. You can read the chat or check the route without losing the meeting time and place. Draw a Route and Add Waypoints With the tablet sideways, the route tools and the waypoint list sit in a panel beside the map. Swipe the panel up or tap Hide to fold it. With the tablet upright, the panel floats in the bottom corner of the map; swipe it down to fold it. Find a Ride Search and the list of rides sit on the left, with the map filling the rest of the screen. Many tablets have no GPS. A Wi-Fi-only tablet can usually only tell roughly where it is, so share your location from your phone on the trail and use the tablet to follow the group.

title: Use Ride Chat
summary: Message everyone on the ride or just the leader, post announcements, and clear or resolve your own messages.
headings: Clear or Resolve Your Own Message
Report or Block Someone in Chat
text: Every ride has its own chat for the riders on it. Use it to plan before the ride and check in after. Only riders who have joined the ride can read or post in it. Don't type while driving or riding. In Ride Mode, use the one-tap quick replies instead. See Send a Status or Quick Reply. Open Ride Chat Open the ride from the Rides tab. Tap Chat in the row of sections under the ride's name. Tap Ride Chat at the top of the card to hide or show the messages. Hidden, it shows the message count and the latest message. The chat shows the newest 30 messages. To see older ones, tap the button above them, such as Show 12 Earlier . Send a Message Under Send To , pick who it's for: Everyone: every rider on the ride. Leader Only: only you and the ride's leader see it. The leader's name is shown on the option. Type in the Message box. Tap Send to Everyone or Send to Leader . Your message shows in the chat straight away as Sending… , then Sent . If it doesn't go through, it stays as Not Sent with Retry and Remove . Messages can be up to 500 characters. If you send more than 10 messages in a minute, you're asked to wait a minute. The ride's leader is every rider with the Leader role. If nobody has been given that role, the organizer leads. Leader-only messages are kept private by the server, not just hidden in the app. If you're the leader, you won't see the Leader Only option. Post an Announcement Organizers and co-organizers can post an announcement for the whole group. Under Send To , pick Announcement (Pinned, Read Aloud) . Type in the Announcement box. Tap Post Announcement . The newest announcement is pinned near the top of the ride page. In Ride Mode it shows as a yellow banner and is read aloud, so riders don't have to look at their phones. Tap the banner to hear it again. Clear or Resolve Your Own Message Tap ••• next to a message you sent. Choose one: Mark Resolved: the message gets a green Resolved tag for everyone. Tap Reopen to undo it. Marking your latest announcement resolved takes it off the pinned spot. Clear: removes the message from the ride chat for everyone. Tap Clear again to confirm. This can't be undone. Only the person who sent a message can clear it or mark it resolved. Quick Replies in Chat Quick replies sent from Ride Mode, like On My Way , also show in the ride chat in italics. Message Pop-Ups When a new message arrives on a ride you're on, a pop-up slides in at the top of the screen, whatever screen you're on. Tap the pop-up to open the ride. Tap Dismiss to close it. When several are waiting, it shows +2 More and Dismiss All . Pop-ups close on their own after a few seconds, and announcements stay up a little longer. If the sender clears a message or marks it resolved before you see it, its pop-up goes away. Pop-ups and notifications follow your choices in Notifications . See Notification Settings. Report or Block Someone in Chat Press and hold someone else's message, then tap Report Rider or Block Rider . See Report or Block a Rider.

title: Your Garage
summary: Add your rig or side-by-side with a photo, fill details from the VIN, track every part of the build and see your fuel range.
headings: Fill In Details From the VIN
text: The Garage keeps your machines in one place: a photo, the details, every part you've added and how far a tank will take you. Open Your Garage Go to the You tab. Under Your Gear , tap Garage . You need to be signed in. Add a Machine Tap Add a Machine . Under What Are You Adding? , pick Vehicle or SXS/UTV . Tap Choose Photo to add a photo from your library (optional). On Android, the system photo picker opens, and OnMyLead only gets the photo you pick. Fill in a Nickname , or the Year , Make and Model . You need a nickname or a make and model. Trim is optional. Add the rest if you like: VIN , Purchase Price ($) , Engine Hours and Odometer (Miles) . Under Fuel and Mileage , enter Tank (gal) , any Extra Fuel (gal) you carry and Miles per Gallon . Use your real-world trail mileage, not the sticker. Tap Add to Garage . Fill In Details From the VIN Type the 17-character VIN . Tap Fill Year, Make and Model From VIN . Check the year, make, model and trim it fills in. If there's no match, enter the details by hand. A VIN is 17 letters and numbers and never uses I, O or Q. See Your Fuel Range Once a machine has a tank size and mpg, its page shows a Fuel Range card: Full Range : how far you can go on your tank plus extra fuel. Safe Turnaround : a third of your full range. Turn around by this many miles out. Safe Trip : two thirds of your full range, the longest round trip that still keeps a third in reserve. It uses the thirds rule: a third out, a third back, a third in reserve. If a machine has no range yet, tap Add Fuel Range . Your Garage also powers the fuel check on a ride. See Fuel Range. Track Your Build Open a machine. Tap Add a Part or Extra . Pick the Area , like Wheels & Tires , Suspension , Lighting or Recovery . Enter the Item , and if you like the Brand , Cost ($) , Installed date (like 2026-05-01) and Notes . Tap Add . Parts are grouped by area with a subtotal for each. At the bottom you'll see the Build Total , and if you entered a purchase price, the Purchase Price and All In total. To change or remove a part, tap it, then tap Save or Remove Item . Export Your Build Under Export on a machine's page: Build Sheet shares your machine and its parts as text, to send in a message or paste anywhere. CSV saves the build list as a spreadsheet file you can send to Files, email or a spreadsheet app. Edit or Delete a Machine Open the machine. Tap Edit Machine to change its details or photo, then tap Save Changes . Or tap Delete , then confirm. The machine and all its build items are removed.

title: Approvals and the Waitlist
summary: How join requests work on rides where the organizer approves riders, and how the waitlist fills open spots on a full ride.
headings: Leaving the Waitlist or a Request
text: Organizers can choose to approve each rider on a public ride, and can cap how many riders or vehicles come along. Here's what happens on both sides. Rides That Need Approval When creating a public ride, the organizer picks I Approve Riders under Joining . See Create a Ride. If You're Asking to Join Open the ride page. Tap Request to Join . The page shows "Your request is waiting for the organizer." You get a notification when you're approved. Until then you don't see the exact meeting point or the group. This is the same whether you found the ride on Find or opened it with its link, QR code or invite code. Only riders the organizer invited through a riding group skip approval. See Invite Riders. If You're the Organizer You get a notification when someone asks to join. Then: Open the ride page. The Riders section shows a red count of requests waiting. Tap Riders . Under Waiting for You , tap Approve or Decline next to each rider. If you set Max Riders or Max Vehicles and the ride is already full, a rider you approve goes on the waitlist instead. They move up automatically when a spot opens. The Waitlist If the organizer set Max Riders or Max Vehicles and the ride is full, new riders go on the waitlist. That includes riders the organizer approves and riders invited through a riding group. The page shows "You're on the waitlist. You'll move up automatically if a spot opens." When a rider leaves, riders on the waitlist move up in the order they joined, as long as they fit. You get a notification when you have a spot. The Spots line on the ride page shows how full the ride is, like "8 of 10 vehicles". Riders on the ride can see how many are on the waitlist under the Going list. Leaving the Waitlist or a Request Open the ride page and tap Leave Ride , or swipe left on the ride on the Rides tab and tap Leave . If the ride is cancelled, riders who asked to join or are on the waitlist get a notification and an email too.

title: Ask the Group with a Ride Poll
summary: Leaders post a quick question in ride chat, like a lunch stop or the pace, and every rider votes with one tap.
text: A ride poll is a quick question in the ride chat with a few choices. Every rider on the ride gets one vote, can change it, and sees the live counts. Who Can Post a Poll The ride's leader, the organizer and co-organizers can post polls. Every rider on the ride can vote. Creating a poll: This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free plan, picking Quick Poll shows Create Ride Polls , marked Pro, instead of the poll form. Voting stays free for everyone. Post a Poll Open the ride and tap Chat . Under Send To , pick Quick Poll . Tap a starter to fill it in, or type your own: Lunch Stop? (Yes, No) How's the Pace? (Too Slow, Just Right, Too Fast) Saturday or Sunday? Morning or Afternoon? Type or edit the Question . Fill in Choice 1 and Choice 2 . Tap Add Choice for more, or Remove to drop one. Tap Post Poll . The poll shows in the chat for everyone, and riders get a pop-up saying "Poll from" your name. Poll Limits 2 to 5 choices, each different. The question can be up to 200 characters. Each choice can be up to 60 characters. Vote Open the ride and tap Chat . Tap a choice. It's marked Your Vote . To change your vote, tap another choice. Each choice shows its count and a bar for its share of the votes, and the leading choice is shaded darker. Under the choices you'll see the total, such as 3 Votes , or No Votes Yet . Remove a Poll The person who posted the poll can tap ••• next to it and tap Clear . The poll and its votes are removed for everyone.

title: Emergencies and Staying Safe
summary: What the EMERGENCY button does and doesn't do, how Need Help works, and how to ride safer with OnMyLead. OnMyLead is not an emergency service.
text: OnMyLead is not an emergency service. It does not contact 911, search and rescue, or anyone outside your ride. If anyone is hurt, call 911 or your local emergency number first. OnMyLead helps your group keep track of each other. Phones lose signal, batteries die, and positions can be late or wrong, so use it alongside your own plan, not instead of one. Everything on this page is free on every plan. None of it needs Pro. What EMERGENCY Does The EMERGENCY button in Ride Mode alerts everyone on your ride at once. In Ride Mode, tap EMERGENCY . It stays on screen even when the bottom panel is folded. Read the Emergency screen. If you're sharing your location, it shows your coordinates in large type, so you can read them out on a call. Press and hold Alert My Group until it sends. A quick tap won't send it. If anyone is hurt, tap Call 911 to open your phone's dialer. Tap Cancel to close the screen without sending anything. When the alert goes out: Every rider on the ride gets a notification, "EMERGENCY: your name needs help now", with "Tap to see where they are." It shows in red on their Ride Mode screen. If you're sharing your location, they see you on the map and can tap Navigate to get directions to you. Help and EMERGENCY notifications are always on for every rider, even in quiet hours, and they come through even from a rider someone has blocked. You see a card showing whose phones have the alert. If you sent it by mistake, tap Cancel on the card and the group is told to ignore it. See Send a Status or Quick Reply. What EMERGENCY Doesn't Do It doesn't call or text 911, emergency services, or anyone else. It doesn't reach anyone who isn't on the ride. It can't send without a connection. With no service, the alert waits on your phone and sends by itself when you get signal. Riders also need service to receive it. Need Help Need Help is for when you need the group but it isn't an emergency. It sends with one tap, shows in red for the group, and notifies everyone on the ride the same way, including during quiet hours. When things are sorted, tap Resolved, I'm OK so the group knows. Ride Safer Call 911 first in an emergency, then alert your group. Share your location for the whole ride , so Ride Bubble and the group can see you, and so riders can find you if you call for help. See Share Your Location. Send a family link to someone at home, and tell them when you expect to be back. See Share a Family Link. Download the ride's map before you lose signal. The map keeps working offline, but positions only update with a connection. See Offline Maps. Allow notifications so you hear when someone needs help. See Notification Settings. Allow location Always , so your group can see you with your phone locked. On Android, allow location While Using the App : the Sharing Your Location notification keeps your group seeing you with the phone locked. Need Help and EMERGENCY arrive in the Rider Alerts notification category, which Android shows at the highest priority. Never type or read the screen while driving or riding. Pull over first. Ride Mode is built for one-tap use when you're stopped. Carry what you need to get yourself home , and ride within your skill and your machine's limits.

title: Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner
summary: Who rides up front, who rides at the rear, and how to make someone leader, pick a tail gunner or hand off the ride.
text: Every group ride needs someone up front and someone at the back. OnMyLead shows the riding order on the roster: the leader first, the tail gunner last, everyone else in between. The Roles Organizer : the rider who created the ride (or was given it). Runs the ride page, starts and ends Ride Mode, and leads unless someone else is made leader. Leader : rides up front. Messages sent to the leader in ride chat go to them. Tail Gunner : rides at the rear so nobody gets left behind. In OnMyLead, the tail gunner is the sweep. Rider : everyone else. On the Riders section of the ride page, the line at the top of the Going list shows who is Leader and who is Tail Gunner (or "Not picked yet"). Make Someone Leader The organizer can put another rider up front while still organizing. On the ride page, tap Riders . Tap the rider's name in the Going list. Tap Make Leader . To take the lead back, tap their name and tap Remove as Leader . You can make more than one rider a leader. Pick a Tail Gunner The organizer or the leader can pick the one rider who rides at the rear. On the ride page, tap Riders . Tap the rider's name. Tap Make Tail Gunner . There's only one tail gunner at a time. Picking someone new moves the job to them. To clear it, tap the tail gunner's name and tap Remove as Tail Gunner . The leader and organizers ride up front, so they can't also be tail gunner. Hand Off the Lead A rider who was made leader can pass the lead to someone else. On the ride page, tap Riders . Tap the rider's name. Tap Hand Them the Lead , then Hand Off . They lead from here, messages to the leader go to them, and you stay on the ride as a rider. Give Away the Whole Ride The organizer can hand the entire ride to another rider, for example if you can't make it. On the ride page, tap Riders . Tap the rider's name. Tap Give Them the Ride , then Give Ride . They become the organizer and the leader. You stay on the ride as a rider and can't undo this yourself. Roles can only go to riders who have joined the ride, and they can't change after the ride has ended or been cancelled. The rider gets a notification when they're made leader, made tail gunner or given the ride.

title: Map Layers and Trails
summary: Switch between satellite and topo, show public trails and roads with their names and closures, and tap a trail to see which vehicles can ride it.
headings: See Who Can Ride a Trail
text: OnMyLead's maps can show public trails and roads over satellite imagery or a topo map. Tap a trail to see its name and which vehicles are allowed on it. Open the Layers The layers button is the round button with a stacked layers icon in the top-right corner of the map. You'll find it on: Ride Mode's map A ride's waypoints map The route builder The area picker for offline maps Tap it to open the Map panel. Tap it again to close the panel. Your choices are remembered on your phone and used on every map in the app. Satellite or Topo At the top of the panel, pick: Satellite : aerial imagery with road and place labels. This is the default. Topo : the USGS topographic map, with contour lines. Public Trails and Roads Turn Public Trails and Roads on to draw trail and road lines on the map. It's on unless you turn it off. Trail : a dashed sand-colored line. Road : a solid pale line. The lines come from: USDA Forest Service : the Motor Vehicle Use Map roads and trails. Bureau of Land Management : BLM routes. OpenStreetMap : tracks mapped by riders, including off-road parks, state land and county roads. Trail lines show once you zoom in. If you see Zoom In to See Trails , zoom in a little. If you see Zoom In for Park and Local Trails , the Forest Service and BLM lines are showing, and the OpenStreetMap tracks appear when you zoom in closer. The map on the Find a Ride tab shows trail lines too when you zoom in, following the choice you made here. See Who Can Ride a Trail Make sure Public Trails and Roads is on and you're zoomed in. Tap a trail or road line. In the route builder, press and hold instead, since a tap adds a route point. A card shows the trail's name, where it is, whether it's a trail, road or track, the segment's miles and surface when known. Under Open To , the card lists the vehicles the agency allows. If access changes by season, it says Open To, by Season with the open dates. If the agency data doesn't say, the card tells you. For an OpenStreetMap track, the card says it was mapped by riders on OpenStreetMap, and that parks and private land need permission or a pass. Map data can be out of date. Always check posted signs and closures before you ride. Download a Ride's Map On a ride with a route, the panel has Download This Ride's Map . One tap saves satellite, topo and trails around the route for riding with no signal. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro and Offline Maps. The Offline Maps link at the bottom of the panel opens all your downloaded maps. With No Signal When your phone loses signal, a No Signal tag with Downloaded Map appears under the layers button. The map then shows only what's saved on your phone, and the satellite view switches to downloaded USGS aerial photos. See Offline Maps. On the Website The website's route builder and waypoints map have the same layers button and Map panel: Satellite or Topo , Public Trails and Roads , the trail and road names, and closed trails in red. The satellite map shows road names too. Zoomed in, the Find a Ride map shows the trail lines and names as well. On the website, click a trail line to see its card when you're not adding points: on a route imported from a GPX file, for example. On the waypoints map a click adds a waypoint, so read the names on the map there. Downloading maps for no signal is only in the app. Map Data and Credits Trails and roads: USDA Forest Service MVUM and Forest Service roads, Bureau of Land Management, and map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, © OpenMapTiles, served by OpenFreeMap. Topo: USGS The National Map. Satellite with no signal: USGS The National Map: Orthoimagery. The credits for what's showing are listed at the bottom of the Map panel. Loading map squares only sends the area being looked at, never anything about you.

title: Plan a Trip and Packing List
summary: Make a packing checklist for a trip, tick things off as they go in the rig, and reset or copy it for next time.
headings: Link a Trip to a Ride
text: The Trip Planner keeps a packing list for each trip. Tick items off as they go in the rig, and reuse the list next time. Open the Trip Planner Go to the You tab. Under Your Gear , tap Trip Planner . You need to be signed in. Plan a New Trip Tap Plan a New Trip . Enter a Trip Name , like "Moab long weekend". Add dates if you like: Starts and Ends , written like 2026-10-12. Ends is optional. If you have machines in your Garage, pick the one you're Taking . Tap Create Trip . Free accounts plan one trip at a time. A trip counts until its last day has passed. Planning several trips at once is part of Pro. See Free and Pro. Add Items On the trip, tap Add an Item . Enter the Item , like "Tow strap". Set How Many with the number box or the minus and plus buttons. Pick a Category , like Recovery , First Aid , Camping or Food & Water . Add Notes if you like, such as size or where it lives in the rig. Tap Add . Items are grouped by category, each showing how many are packed. Start From a Starter List Tap Add a Starter List and pick one, like Day Ride , Overnight / Camping , Desert , Mountain / Snow , Recovery Kit , First Aid , Tools & Spares or Starlink / Power . One tap adds the items. You can add more than one list, and nothing is added twice. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Tick Items Off Tap anywhere on an item's row to check it off. Tap again to uncheck it. The bar at the top shows how much is packed. When everything is checked, it turns green and says so, like All 24 packed. To change or remove an item, tap Edit on its row, then tap Save or Remove Item . After the Trip Under After the Trip : Uncheck All puts every item back to not packed. The list stays. Copy to a New Trip starts a new trip with the same list. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Link a Trip to a Ride When you create or edit a trip, you can pick a ride you've joined under For a Ride . The trip then shows a link to that ride. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Edit or Delete a Trip Open the trip. Tap Edit Trip to change the name, dates, machine or ride, then tap Save . Or tap Delete , then confirm. The trip and all its items are removed. Gear Suggestions A trip's page may show Gear From RUS Offroad , with products that fit your list and machine. See Gear From RUS Offroad.

title: Redeem a Promo Code
summary: Got an OnMyLead promo code? Redeem it in the app through Apple to get OnMyLead Pro with the offer it includes.
headings: Redeem a Code in the App
Redeemed It in the App Store Instead?
text: OnMyLead promo codes are Apple offer codes for OnMyLead Pro. You redeem them through Apple, right from the app. Redeem a Code in the App On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Redeem Promo Code . Enter your code in Apple's window and follow the steps to confirm. Apple shows what the code gives you before you confirm. Once Apple accepts the code, OnMyLead checks it and your plan changes to Pro . This can take a moment. You can also tap Redeem Promo Code at the bottom of the Pro screen. Redeem a Code on Android On Android, OnMyLead promo codes are Google Play promo codes. On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Redeem Promo Code . Google Play's Redeem Code page opens. Enter your code and follow the steps to confirm. Come back to OnMyLead. Once Google Play has the code, your plan changes to Pro . You can also redeem a code in the Play Store app: tap your profile picture, then Payments & Subscriptions Redeem Code . A Google Play code works only on Google Play, and an Apple offer code works only in the App Store. Redeemed It in the App Store Instead? That works too. Open OnMyLead afterwards, signed in to your account, with signal. The app picks up the code on its own and turns on Pro. Good to Know A promo code becomes an OnMyLead Pro subscription with your Apple Account. Manage or cancel it like any subscription. See Manage or Cancel Your Subscription. Promo codes can only be redeemed in the app on your phone or tablet, not on the website. If your plan doesn't change to Pro, make sure you have signal and are signed in to the right OnMyLead account, then tap Restore Purchases . See Restore Purchases.

title: Check In
summary: Let the group know you've made it to the meeting spot with one tap, and see who's already there.
text: Checking in tells the organizer and the rest of the group that you're at the meeting spot and ready to ride. Check In Open the ride page. Tap I'm Here and Ready . The button changes to "Checked in at" and the time you tapped it. You can check in once you've joined the ride, until the ride ends. Checking in doesn't use your location. It does need a connection, so if the trailhead has no signal, check in before you lose it. See Who's Here On the ride page, tap Riders . Riders who checked in show Here under their name in the Going list. Organizers use this to see who's made it before starting Ride Mode. Once you've checked in, you can't undo it. Need help getting to the meeting spot? Directions are on the ride page once you've joined. See Directions.

title: Offline Maps
summary: Download a ride's map or any area before you leave, so the map and route are still there when the signal drops. A Pro feature.
text: Out on the trail the signal often drops. Download a map before you leave and the map keeps working with no signal: satellite photos, topo and trail lines for the area you saved. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Maps already on your phone keep working on the Free plan. Offline maps keep the map, not the tracking. With no signal, your phone can't send or receive positions. Riders show where they were last seen, and positions update again when phones get a connection. Offline maps are in the app on your phone or tablet only, not on the website. Open Offline Maps On the You tab, tap Offline Maps . Or, on any map with the layers button, open the layers panel and tap Offline Maps . The screen shows how much space your maps use, how much is free on your phone, your downloads under On This Phone , and your upcoming rides under Your Rides . Download a Ride's Map The quickest way. It saves satellite, topo and trails around the ride's route. From Offline Maps: Under Your Rides , find the ride. Each one shows about how much space it needs. Tap Download . From the ride's map: Open Ride Mode or the ride's waypoints map. Tap the layers button. Tap Download This Ride's Map . Your Rides lists upcoming rides you've joined that have a mapped route. Downloading a ride again replaces its earlier download, which is handy if the route changed. Download Any Area On Offline Maps, tap Download a Map Area . Move and zoom the map until the frame holds the area you'll ride. The frame's size in miles shows in its corner. Pick the maps to save: Satellite , Topo and Trails . All three are on to start. Check the estimate under the choices. Tap Download This Area . The download is named after the nearest town when your phone can find one. If you see Too big for one download. Zoom in a little. , the area is too large to save with enough detail to ride by. Zoom in, or save it as two downloads. Watch and Manage Downloads Each download on On This Phone shows its maps, its size and how it's going. Pause stops a download for now. Resume carries on from where it stopped. Finish appears when some pieces didn't download. The download shows how many are missing; tap Finish to try them again. Delete takes it off your phone. Tap Delete again to confirm, or Keep . One download runs at a time. If you close the app during a download, it's paused; open Offline Maps and tap Resume . Deleting a download only removes pieces that no other download also uses, so overlapping maps keep working. When the Signal Drops You don't need to do anything. The app checks for a connection while a map is open. When it can't reach the internet: A No Signal tag with Downloaded Map appears under the layers button. The map shows what's saved on your phone. Zoomed in past what you saved, it stretches the closest saved detail. The satellite view switches to USGS aerial photos from your download, since the live satellite view can't be saved ahead of time. The ride's route and waypoints are saved on your phone once you've opened the ride, so they're still on the map too. Download before you leave, while you have good signal. Then open the ride once so its route is on your phone. What Gets Saved Satellite : USGS aerial photos. Topo : the USGS topo map. Trails : Forest Service and BLM lines, plus OpenStreetMap tracks (map data © OpenStreetMap contributors). Trail and topo areas you've already looked at with signal are also kept on your phone for a while, but only a download makes sure the whole area is there. If Your Pro Plan Ends Maps you already downloaded stay on your phone and keep working. Starting a new download needs Pro.

title: Restore Purchases
summary: Bring your OnMyLead Pro subscription back after getting a new iPhone, reinstalling the app, or signing in again.
headings: If It Says No Purchase Was Found
text: If you pay for OnMyLead Pro but your plan shows Free, for example on a new iPhone or after reinstalling the app, use Restore Purchases . It finds your Pro subscription with Apple and turns Pro back on. Restore Your Subscription Sign in to your OnMyLead account. On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Restore Purchases . If Apple asks, sign in with the Apple Account you used to buy Pro. When it works, the app says Your Pro subscription is restored. and your plan shows Pro . You can also tap Restore Purchases at the bottom of the Pro screen. If It Says No Purchase Was Found The app says No OnMyLead Pro purchase found for this Apple ID. when the Apple Account on this iPhone has no active OnMyLead Pro subscription. Check that: You're signed in to the same Apple Account you used to subscribe. The subscription is still active. Look in iPhone Settings your name Subscriptions . You have signal. Restore on Android On Android, Restore Purchases looks for OnMyLead Pro on the Google account signed in to the Play Store. If it finds none, the app says No OnMyLead Pro purchase found for this Google account. Check that the Play Store is signed in to the Google account you used to subscribe, and that the subscription is still active in the Play Store app under Payments & Subscriptions Subscriptions . You don't need to restore on a different kind of device. Pro bought on an iPhone shows on your Android phone or tablet as soon as you sign in to the same OnMyLead account, and the other way round. One Subscription, One Account An Apple subscription gives Pro to one OnMyLead account at a time. If you restore it while signed in to a different OnMyLead account, Pro moves to that account. Make sure you're signed in to the account you want Pro on before you tap Restore Purchases . Restore Purchases works in the app only, on iPhone, iPad or Android. Once Pro is on your account, it also works when you use OnMyLead on the website.

title: Ride Day and Weather
summary: See the forecast for the meeting area and check whether your ride gets back before sunset, right on the ride page.
text: The Ride Day card on the ride page shows the weather for the meeting area and how your ride lines up with daylight, so nobody gets surprised by a storm or the last miles in the dark. Where to Find It Open the ride page. Ride Day is in the Details section. It shows on upcoming and live rides. The Forecast Ride Day shows the meet day's forecast: The conditions, such as Clear, Partly Cloudy, Rain or Thunderstorms The high and low temperature The chance of rain The wind speed, and gusts when they're much stronger than the wind The forecast shows up about two weeks before the ride. Until then the card says when it will appear. The forecast is for the ride's general meeting area, not the exact spot. The last forecast your phone loaded is saved, so it still shows at a trailhead with no signal. It only updates when you have a connection. Weather Warnings Ride Day adds a heads-up when the forecast calls for: Thunderstorms (watch for lightning and flash floods in washes) A 60% or higher chance of rain Gusts of 35 mph or more A high of 100°F or more A low of 32°F or below Daylight Check Ride Day shows sunrise and sunset at the meeting area, with a bar that shows when the ride runs against the daylight. If the ride has a Back By time (the Expected Finish you set when creating the ride), Ride Day tells you: How long before sunset the group is back When it's cutting it close: back less than 45 minutes before sunset When the group will be back after dark, with a reminder to bring lights If there's no finish time, the card says to add a Back By time so it can check it against sunset. Countdown At the top of an upcoming ride's page, a tag counts down to the meeting time, such as "Tomorrow", "In 4 Days" or "Starts in 25 min".

title: Starlink Dish Status and Power Planner
summary: See your Starlink dish's live status on its Wi-Fi, keep your plan details handy, and work out how long your batteries will run it.
headings: If It Can't Reach Your Dish
text: The Starlink page shows how your dish is doing, keeps your plan details in one place, and works out how long your batteries will run it. Open the Starlink Page Go to the You tab. Under On the Trail , tap Starlink . See Your Dish's Live Status Join your Starlink's Wi-Fi network on your iPhone. On the Starlink page, tap Connect to My Dish . If your iPhone asks to let OnMyLead find devices on your local network, allow it. While the page is open, Your Dish stays live and shows: Whether the dish is online, and its current state. Download Now , Upload Now and Latency . Sky Blocked , Dropped Pings and Up For . Any alerts from the dish. The last 15 minutes as a bar chart, with dropouts in red. Where the dish is facing, GPS, and its software and hardware versions. After the first time, the page reconnects by itself when you open it. It stops reading the dish when you leave the page. This uses your dish's built-in local connection, which SpaceX doesn't officially support. A Starlink update can break it. Everything else on the page keeps working. If It Can't Reach Your Dish If you see Can't Reach Your Dish : Make sure your iPhone is on your Starlink Wi-Fi. Allow local network access in your iPhone's Settings , under OnMyLead . The page keeps trying every 10 seconds. Tap Retry Now to try straight away. If it says your dish answered but couldn't be read, a Starlink software update may have changed things. Try again later. Reading the dish only works in the iPhone app, not on the website. Save Your Plan Starlink doesn't share plan or usage details with other apps, so you can jot them down here. Check your usage in the Starlink app. If you have machines in your Garage, pick one under Setup For , or General . Each one keeps its own setup. Under My Plan , fill in Plan , Monthly Cost ($) and Data Cap (GB) . Pick your Dish and what it's Powered By . Add Notes like your mount, cable length or router settings. Tap Save . You need to be signed in to save. Plan Your Power Under Power Budget : Enter your Dish Watts . If you picked your dish, the typical range is shown. Enter Hours per Day you'll run it. Under Battery Size In , choose Watt-Hours or Amp-Hours + Volts , then enter your battery size. Set Usable % . Use about 90 for lithium and 50 for lead-acid. If you have solar, enter Solar Watts and Sun Hours per day. The page shows your Battery Runtime , what the Dish Uses / Day , what Solar Adds / Day , and your daily balance in green or red. These are estimates. Snow melt, heat and heavy use draw more power. You can use the power calculator without signing in, but you need to sign in to save it.

title: Gear From RUS Offroad
summary: Why you may see product suggestions from RUS Offroad on your machine's page and your trip packing list, and how they're picked.
text: OnMyLead is made by RUS Offroad. In a couple of places, the app may suggest RUS Offroad products that fit your machine or your packing list. The section is always labeled Gear From RUS Offroad . Where You'll See It On one of your machines in your Garage, with products that fit that machine. On a trip in the Trip Planner, with products that fit your packing list and the machine you're taking. Each suggestion shows the product, its price and how it fits, like "Fits your" followed by your machine, or "Fits most machines." Buy or Browse Tap Buy to open that product on the RUS Offroad store inside the app. Tap Shop more at rusoffroad.com to browse the whole store. Purchases happen on the RUS Offroad website, not through OnMyLead or your Apple subscription. When It Doesn't Show The section only appears when something fits. You won't see it if nothing matches, if the store can't be reached, or if suggestions are switched off for a while.

title: Get Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
summary: Hand off to Apple Maps or Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions to the meeting point, along the route, to the destination, or to a rider.
headings: Get Directions to the Meeting Point
text: OnMyLead hands you over to Apple Maps or Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions on the road. Off road, follow the leader and the route on the OnMyLead map. On Android, directions open in Google Maps, since Android phones and tablets don't have Apple Maps. Only the place you want to go is sent to the maps app, nothing about you. Get Directions to the Meeting Point Open the ride from the Rides tab. On the Details section, find the Directions card. Tap a row: Meeting Point: the exact meeting spot. Along the Route: follows the ride's route through stops on the way, ending at the end of the route. Destination: the ride's destination, if the organizer added one. Pick Apple Maps or Google Maps , unless you've already chosen one (below). The Directions card shows while the ride is scheduled or live. Meeting Point and Along the Route only show for riders who have joined the ride, because the exact meeting spot and the route are private to them. See Privacy. Get Directions in Ride Mode In Ride Mode, tap Directions just above the bottom panel, on the left. Tap a row: Regroup Point: where the leader asked everyone to meet up, when one is set. Meeting Point Continue Along the Route: picks up from where you are on the route. Destination Pick your maps app, if asked. You can also get directions from other places in Ride Mode: Tap the yellow Regroup point set. Tap to navigate banner. Tap Navigate on a rider's alert card. Open the Riders list and tap Navigate , or Go to Last Seen for a rider whose position is old. Tap a waypoint on the map. See Waypoints and Planned Stops. Directions along the route pass through up to 8 stops picked from the route, and the maps app keeps to roads it knows between them. Off-road parts of the route may differ, so follow the OnMyLead map there. Choose Your Maps App Tap the You tab. Under Settings , tap Directions . Pick Ask Each Time , Apple Maps or Google Maps . Tap Done . Every Navigate and Directions button in the app uses this choice. With Ask Each Time , the app asks which one to open every time. Google Maps opens in its app if you have it installed, and in your browser if you don't.

title: Ride Summary and Ride Again
summary: After a ride ends, see your distance and route, who finished, share a ride card, and set up the same ride again in a few taps.
text: When the organizer ends a ride, everyone who was on it gets a summary on the ride page. Organizers can also start the same ride again with one tap. See Your Ride Summary On the Rides tab, find the ride under Past Rides . Tap it. The summary is at the top of the ride page. The summary has three parts. Your Ride Your Distance and how long you were Out For , plus a map of your route. Only you can see your route. Your stats come from sharing your location in Ride Mode. If you didn't share, there's no track for you on that ride. See Location Sharing. Moving Time , Average Speed , Top Speed and Climbing are part of Advanced Ride Statistics. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Your full stats are saved either way. The Group Who finished the ride: the riders still on it when it ended. With Pro, you also see the group's totals: the Longest and Average distance and the Group Top Speed . These are totals only, and nobody's route is shown. Ride Card A picture of the ride to share with friends or on social media. Pick a layout: Standard , Full Stats or Big Number . Tap Share Ride Card . Standard is free. Full Stats and Big Number are Premium Ride Cards. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. The card never shows the meeting point or anyone's route. Ride Again Organizers can set up the same ride again without filling everything in. Open the ended ride's page. In the You're Organizing card, tap Ride Again . The Create a Ride form opens with the name, details, meeting point and route already filled in. The day is set to the next one on the same weekday. Check the day and times. Tap Create Public Ride or Create Private Ride . On a ride that hasn't ended yet, the same button is called Copy This Ride . Ride Again creates a new ride, so it counts toward your monthly rides on Free. See Create a Ride. Advanced Ride Statistics, Premium Ride Cards and full ride history work with Pro from either store: the App Store on iPhone and iPad, or Google Play on Android. Past Rides Ended and cancelled rides move to Past Rides on the Rides tab. Free shows your last 5. Full ride history is a Pro feature. Nothing is deleted, so older rides show again with Pro. See Free and Pro. To remove a ride from your Past Rides, swipe left on it and tap Leave (or Delete if you organized it). On onmylead.com, click the button at the end of the ride's row instead.

title: Search for a Place
summary: Find a trailhead, off-road park, town, street address or coordinates for a meeting point, a destination or the map.
text: Wherever OnMyLead asks for a place, you can type its name instead of hunting on a map: a trailhead, an off-road park, a campground, a town or a street address. Where You Can Search Creating a ride : Search a Place or Address sets the meeting point, and Search a Destination fills in where the ride ends up. See Create a Ride. Find a Ride : Search Near a Place shows rides near the place you pick instead of near you. Tap Back to Near Me (or Clear ) to go back. See Find a Ride. Route builder : Search moves the map to a place before you draw. See Draw a Route. Search Tap the search box and type at least three letters. Results show as you type. Each one says what it is and where, like "Trailhead in Moab, Utah". Tap the one you want. What happens next depends on where you searched: For a meeting point, the coordinates and place name fill in for you. You can still edit the Place Name . In the route builder, the map moves to the place and marks it. Nothing is added to your route. If nothing turns up, try the full name, a street address with the town, or a nearby town. Search by Coordinates Type coordinates as latitude and longitude, like 38.5733, -109.5498 , and pick the result. This works for spots that don't have a name. Good to Know Search covers places in the United States. Results near you, or near where the map is looking, come first. Search needs a connection. With no signal you'll see No signal for place search. Try again with service. Only the words you type and a rough area are sent to the search service, never who you are or your exact location. On the Website The same searches work on onmylead.com. When you create a ride on the website, you can also click the map to drop the meeting point and drag the pin to fine-tune it. See Create a Ride on the Website. Place Data Places come from OpenStreetMap (map data © OpenStreetMap contributors), searched through Photon, a free service with no account.

title: Delete Your Account
summary: Permanently delete your OnMyLead account and its data from the You tab, and what to do about a Pro subscription first.
text: You can delete your OnMyLead account yourself, right in the app. It happens straight away and can't be undone. Before You Delete If you pay for OnMyLead Pro, cancel it with Apple too. Apple bills the subscription, so deleting your account doesn't stop it. See Manage Your Subscription. Delete Your Account Go to the You tab. Scroll to the bottom and tap Delete Account . Read the message, then tap Delete Account to confirm. You're signed out and taken back to the start. What Gets Deleted Your account and profile. Rides you organize. They're removed for everyone on them. Your Garage, trips and riding groups. Your messages and location history. This can't be undone. To ride with OnMyLead again later, you'd make a new account. If You See Deletion Requested Sometimes the app shows Deletion Requested instead of signing you out. That means your request was sent and your account and its data will be deleted within 7 days. If you pay for Pro, cancel it in your Apple subscriptions so you aren't billed again. Need Help? If the delete doesn't go through, Contact Us and pick Account and Sign-In .
